source_arguments.name: RHTower.exists_separated_primeLog_nodes_growing
source_arguments.statement:
theorem exists_separated_primeLog_nodes_growing {c₁ : ℝ} (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) :
    ∃ R₀ : ℝ, ∀ R : ℝ, R₀ ≤ R →
      ∃ s : Finset ℝ, s.card = ⌊c₁ * R⌋₊ + 1 ∧
        ↑s ⊆ Set.Icc R (R + 1) ∧
        (∀ t ∈ s, ∀ u ∈ s, t ≠ u →
          1 / (4 * ((⌊c₁ * R⌋₊ : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ |t - u|) ∧
        (∀ t ∈ s, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ t = Real.log p)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem exists_separated_primeLog_nodes_growing {c₁ : ℝ} (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) :
    ∃ R₀ : ℝ, ∀ R : ℝ, R₀ ≤ R →
      ∃ s : Finset ℝ, s.card = ⌊c₁ * R⌋₊ + 1 ∧
        ↑s ⊆ Set.Icc R (R + 1) ∧
        (∀ t ∈ s, ∀ u ∈ s, t ≠ u →
          1 / (4 * ((⌊c₁ * R⌋₊ : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ |t - u|) ∧
        (∀ t ∈ s, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ t = Real.log p)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨c₂, K, y₀, hc₂, hK, hy₀3, hwin⟩ :=
    exists_prime_log_in_shrinking_window
  obtain ⟨Rh, hRh0, hRh⟩ :=
    exists_linear_le_exp_rpow (a := 4 * K * (c₁ + 1)) (b := c₂)
      (by positivity) hc₂
  refine ⟨max y₀ Rh, fun R hR => ?_⟩
  have hRy₀ : y₀ ≤ R := le_trans (le_max_left _ _) hR
  have hRRh : Rh ≤ R := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) hR
  have hR0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ R := le_trans (by linarith) hRy₀
  set N : ℕ := ⌊c₁ * R⌋₊ with hN
  have hNc : (N : ℝ) ≤ c₁ * R := by
    rw [hN]; exact Nat.floor_le (by positivity)
  have hN10 : (0 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) + 1 := by positivity
  set η : ℝ := 1 / (4 * ((N : ℝ) + 1)) with hη
  have hη0 : 0 < η := by positivity
  have hη1 : η ≤ 1 := by
    rw [hη, div_le_one (by positivity)]
    have hNn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg N
    linarith
  -- the master threshold `4K(c₁R+1) ≤ exp(c₂ R^{1/10})`
  have hthresh : 4 * K * (c₁ * R + 1)
      ≤ Real.exp (c₂ * R ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10)) := by
    have h1 := hRh R hRRh
    have h2 : 4 * K * (c₁ * R + 1)
        ≤ 4 * K * (c₁ + 1) * (R + 1) := by
      have hKpos : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 4 * K := by positivity
      nlinarith [mul_nonneg hKpos hR0, hK.le, hc₁.le, hR0]
    linarith
  -- hence `K·exp(-c₂ R^{1/10}) ≤ 1/(4(c₁R+1))`
  have hKR : K * Real.exp (-(c₂ * R ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10)))
      ≤ 1 / (4 * (c₁ * R + 1)) := by
    rw [Real.exp_neg, mul_inv_le_iff₀ (Real.exp_pos _)]
    rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
    nlinarith [hthresh]
  -- `1/(4(c₁R+1)) ≤ η`
  have hηlb : 1 / (4 * (c₁ * R + 1)) ≤ η := by
    rw [hη]
    apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by positivity)
    have : (N : ℝ) + 1 ≤ c₁ * R + 1 := by linarith
    linarith
  -- supply a prime in each shrinking window
  have hwindows : ∀ i : Fin (N + 1), ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧
      R + 4 * (1 / (4 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))) * (i : ℕ) ≤ Real.log p ∧
      Real.log p ≤ R + 4 * (1 / (4 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))) * (i : ℕ)
        + 1 / (4 * ((N : ℝ) + 1)) := by
    intro i
    set yi : ℝ := R + 4 * (1 / (4 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))) * (i : ℕ) with hyi
    have hyi_ge : R ≤ yi := by
      rw [hyi]
      have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 4 * (1 / (4 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))) * (i : ℕ) := by
        positivity
      linarith
    have hyi_y₀ : y₀ ≤ yi := le_trans hRy₀ hyi_ge
    -- the shrinking-window threshold at `yi`
    have hyipow : R ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10) ≤ yi ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10) :=
      Real.rpow_le_rpow hR0 hyi_ge (by norm_num)
    have hEyi : K * Real.exp (-(c₂ * yi ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10))) ≤ η := by
      have hmono : Real.exp (-(c₂ * yi ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10)))
          ≤ Real.exp (-(c₂ * R ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10))) := by
        apply Real.exp_le_exp.2
        have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hyipow hc₂.le
        linarith
      calc K * Real.exp (-(c₂ * yi ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10)))
          ≤ K * Real.exp (-(c₂ * R ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10))) :=
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hmono hK.le
        _ ≤ 1 / (4 * (c₁ * R + 1)) := hKR
        _ ≤ η := hηlb
    have hηyi : K * Real.exp (-(c₂ * yi ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10)))
        ≤ 1 / (4 * ((N : ℝ) + 1)) := by rw [← hη]; exact hEyi
    obtain ⟨p, hp, h1, h2⟩ := hwin yi (1 / (4 * ((N : ℝ) + 1)))
      hyi_y₀ (by rw [← hη]; exact hη0) (by rw [← hη]; exact hη1) hηyi
    exact ⟨p, hp, h1, h2⟩
  -- assemble via the banked node-assembly theorem
  exact exists_separated_primeLog_nodes hwindows

theorem PairWord.norm_forwardProduct_le {n L m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    {kappa rho M : ℝ} (hkappa : 0 < kappa) (hrho : 0 < rho)
    (hkappaRho : kappa ≤ rho) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (W : PairWord n L) (hm : ∀ i j, i < j → W.pairMultiplicity i j ≤ m)
    (F : Fin L → ℂ → A)
    (hupper : ∀ r, DiffContOnHorizontalCl (F r) 0 rho)
    (hlower : ∀ r, DiffContOnHorizontalCl (F r) (-rho) 0)
    (hreal : ∀ r (x : ℝ), ‖F r x‖ ≤ 1)
    (hstrip : ∀ r z, |z.im| ≤ rho → ‖F r z‖ ≤ M)
    {zeta : Fin n → ℂ} (hzeta : InShrinkingTube kappa zeta) :
    ‖W.forwardProduct F zeta‖ ≤ M ^ (m * kappa * (n - 1 : ℕ) / (2 * rho))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem PairWord.norm_forwardProduct_le {n L m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    {kappa rho M : ℝ} (hkappa : 0 < kappa) (hrho : 0 < rho)
    (hkappaRho : kappa ≤ rho) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (W : PairWord n L) (hm : ∀ i j, i < j → W.pairMultiplicity i j ≤ m)
    (F : Fin L → ℂ → A)
    (hupper : ∀ r, DiffContOnHorizontalCl (F r) 0 rho)
    (hlower : ∀ r, DiffContOnHorizontalCl (F r) (-rho) 0)
    (hreal : ∀ r (x : ℝ), ‖F r x‖ ≤ 1)
    (hstrip : ∀ r z, |z.im| ≤ rho → ‖F r z‖ ≤ M)
    {zeta : Fin n → ℂ} (hzeta : InShrinkingTube kappa zeta) :
    ‖W.forwardProduct F zeta‖ ≤ M ^ (m * kappa * (n - 1 : ℕ) / (2 * rho))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let e : Fin L → ℝ := fun r =>
    |(zeta (W.left r) - zeta (W.right r)).im| / rho
  have hnR : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hkdiv : kappa / (n : ℝ) ≤ rho :=
    (div_le_self hkappa.le hnR).trans hkappaRho
  have hfactor : ∀ r : Fin L,
      ‖F r (zeta (W.left r) - zeta (W.right r))‖ ≤ M ^ e r := by
    intro r
    apply norm_le_rpow_abs_im_div_of_horizontal_threeLines hrho hM
      (hupper r) (hlower r) (hreal r) (hstrip r)
    exact (abs_im_sub_lt_of_mem_shrinkingTube hzeta (W.left r) (W.right r)).le.trans hkdiv
  have hprod := norm_orderedWordProduct_le_rpow_sum
    (List.ofFn fun r : Fin L => r)
    (fun r => F r (zeta (W.left r) - zeta (W.right r))) hM e
    (fun r _ => hfactor r)
  have hsum := W.factorExponent_sum_le hn hkappa hrho hm hzeta
  have hsumE : (((List.ofFn fun r : Fin L => r).map e).sum) ≤
      m * kappa * (n - 1 : ℕ) / (2 * rho) := by
    simpa [e, List.map_ofFn, Function.comp_def] using hsum
  have hpow := Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hM hsumE
  exact (by
    simpa [PairWord.forwardProduct, e, List.map_ofFn, Function.comp_def] using
      hprod.trans hpow)

    {y : ℂ → ℂ} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    {kappa rho M : ℝ} (hkappa : 0 < kappa) (hrho : 0 < rho)
    (hkappaRho : kappa ≤ rho) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hupper : DiffContOnHorizontalCl y 0 rho)
    (hlower : DiffContOnHorizontalCl y (-rho) 0)
    (hreal : ∀ x : ℝ, ‖y x‖ ≤ 1)
    (hstrip : ∀ z, |z.im| ≤ rho → ‖y z‖ ≤ M)
    {zeta : Fin n → ℂ} (hzeta : InShrinkingTube kappa zeta) :
    ‖analyticPairMultiplier y zeta‖ ≤ pairWordHardyBase M 1 kappa rho ^ n
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem norm_analyticPairMultiplier_le_hardyBase_pow
    {y : ℂ → ℂ} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    {kappa rho M : ℝ} (hkappa : 0 < kappa) (hrho : 0 < rho)
    (hkappaRho : kappa ≤ rho) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hupper : DiffContOnHorizontalCl y 0 rho)
    (hlower : DiffContOnHorizontalCl y (-rho) 0)
    (hreal : ∀ x : ℝ, ‖y x‖ ≤ 1)
    (hstrip : ∀ z, |z.im| ≤ rho → ‖y z‖ ≤ M)
    {zeta : Fin n → ℂ} (hzeta : InShrinkingTube kappa zeta) :
    ‖analyticPairMultiplier y zeta‖ ≤ pairWordHardyBase M 1 kappa rho ^ n
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let e : ℝ := kappa / ((n : ℝ) * rho)
  have hnR : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hkdiv : kappa / (n : ℝ) ≤ rho :=
    (div_le_self hkappa.le hnR).trans hkappaRho
  have heNonneg : 0 ≤ e := by positivity
  have hfactor : ∀ (l : Fin n) (k : Fin l),
      ‖y (zeta (Fin.castLE l.isLt.le k) - zeta l)‖ ≤ M ^ e := by
    intro l k
    let i : Fin n := Fin.castLE l.isLt.le k
    have him := (abs_im_sub_lt_of_mem_shrinkingTube hzeta i l).le
    have hthree := norm_le_rpow_abs_im_div_of_horizontal_threeLines
      hrho hM hupper hlower hreal hstrip (zeta i - zeta l) (him.trans hkdiv)
    exact hthree.trans (Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hM (by
      dsimp [e]
      calc
        |(zeta i - zeta l).im| / rho ≤ (kappa / (n : ℝ)) / rho :=
          div_le_div_of_nonneg_right him hrho.le
        _ = kappa / ((n : ℝ) * rho) := by rw [div_div]))
  have hinner : ∀ l : Fin n,
      ‖∏ k : Fin l, y (zeta (Fin.castLE l.isLt.le k) - zeta l)‖ ≤ (M ^ e) ^ l.val := by
    intro l
    rw [norm_prod]
    calc
      ∏ k : Fin l, ‖y (zeta (Fin.castLE l.isLt.le k) - zeta l)‖
          ≤ ∏ _k : Fin l, M ^ e :=
            Finset.prod_le_prod (fun _ _ => norm_nonneg _) (fun k _ => hfactor l k)
      _ = (M ^ e) ^ l.val := by simp
  rw [analyticPairMultiplier, norm_prod]
  calc
    ∏ l : Fin n, ‖∏ k : Fin l, y (zeta (Fin.castLE l.isLt.le k) - zeta l)‖
        ≤ ∏ l : Fin n, (M ^ e) ^ l.val :=
          Finset.prod_le_prod (fun _ _ => norm_nonneg _) (fun l _ => hinner l)
    _ = (M ^ e) ^ n.choose 2 := by
      rw [Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum]
      congr 1
      calc
        ∑ i : Fin n, i.val = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, i :=
          Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i : ℕ => i) n
        _ = n * (n - 1) / 2 := Finset.sum_range_id n
        _ = n.choose 2 := (Nat.choose_two_right n).symm
    _ = M ^ (kappa * (n - 1 : ℕ) / (2 * rho)) := by
      rw [← Real.rpow_natCast]
      rw [← Real.rpow_mul (zero_le_one.trans hM)]
      congr 1
      dsimp [e]
      have hchoose : (2 : ℝ) * n.choose 2 = (n : ℝ) * (n - 1 : ℕ) := by
        exact_mod_cast two_mul_choose_two_eq_mul_pred_scalarCDD n
      field_simp
      nlinarith
    _ ≤ pairWordHardyBase M 1 kappa rho ^ n := by
      simpa using rpow_pairWordExponent_le_hardyBase_pow
        (n := n) (m := 1) hM hkappa hrho

theorem PairWord.norm_inverseProduct_le {n L m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    {kappa rho M : ℝ} (hkappa : 0 < kappa) (hrho : 0 < rho)
    (hkappaRho : kappa ≤ rho) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (W : PairWord n L) (hm : ∀ i j, i < j → W.pairMultiplicity i j ≤ m)
    (G : Fin L → ℂ → A)
    (hupper : ∀ r, DiffContOnHorizontalCl (G r) 0 rho)
    (hlower : ∀ r, DiffContOnHorizontalCl (G r) (-rho) 0)
    (hreal : ∀ r (x : ℝ), ‖G r x‖ ≤ 1)
    (hstrip : ∀ r z, |z.im| ≤ rho → ‖G r z‖ ≤ M)
    {zeta : Fin n → ℂ} (hzeta : InShrinkingTube kappa zeta) :
    ‖W.inverseProduct G zeta‖ ≤ M ^ (m * kappa * (n - 1 : ℕ) / (2 * rho))

theorem PairWord.norm_inverseProduct_le {n L m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    {kappa rho M : ℝ} (hkappa : 0 < kappa) (hrho : 0 < rho)
    (hkappaRho : kappa ≤ rho) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (W : PairWord n L) (hm : ∀ i j, i < j → W.pairMultiplicity i j ≤ m)
    (G : Fin L → ℂ → A)
    (hupper : ∀ r, DiffContOnHorizontalCl (G r) 0 rho)
    (hlower : ∀ r, DiffContOnHorizontalCl (G r) (-rho) 0)
    (hreal : ∀ r (x : ℝ), ‖G r x‖ ≤ 1)
    (hstrip : ∀ r z, |z.im| ≤ rho → ‖G r z‖ ≤ M)
    {zeta : Fin n → ℂ} (hzeta : InShrinkingTube kappa zeta) :
    ‖W.inverseProduct G zeta‖ ≤ M ^ (m * kappa * (n - 1 : ℕ) / (2 * rho))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let e : Fin L → ℝ := fun r =>
    |(zeta (W.left r) - zeta (W.right r)).im| / rho
  have hnR : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hkdiv : kappa / (n : ℝ) ≤ rho :=
    (div_le_self hkappa.le hnR).trans hkappaRho
  have hfactor : ∀ r : Fin L,
      ‖G r (zeta (W.left r) - zeta (W.right r))‖ ≤ M ^ e r := by
    intro r
    apply norm_le_rpow_abs_im_div_of_horizontal_threeLines hrho hM
      (hupper r) (hlower r) (hreal r) (hstrip r)
    exact (abs_im_sub_lt_of_mem_shrinkingTube hzeta (W.left r) (W.right r)).le.trans hkdiv
  have hprod := norm_orderedWordProduct_le_rpow_sum
    (List.ofFn fun r : Fin L => r).reverse
    (fun r => G r (zeta (W.left r) - zeta (W.right r))) hM e
    (fun r _ => hfactor r)
  have hsum := W.factorExponent_sum_le hn hkappa hrho hm hzeta
  have hsumReverse :
      (((List.ofFn fun r : Fin L => r).reverse.map e).sum) =
        (List.ofFn e).sum := by
    simp [List.map_reverse, List.map_ofFn, Function.comp_def]
  have hpow := Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hM hsum
  rw [← hsumReverse] at hpow
  simpa [PairWord.inverseProduct, reverseWordProduct, orderedWordProduct,
    List.map_reverse, List.map_ofFn, Function.comp_def] using hprod.trans hpow

theorem continuous_parametric_primitive_of_continuous

source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem continuous_parametric_primitive_of_continuous
    {a₀ : ℝ} (hf : Continuous f.uncurry) :
    Continuous fun p : X × ℝ ↦ ∫ t in a₀..p.2, f p.1 t ∂μ
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  -- We will prove continuity at a point `(q, b₀)`.
  rw [continuous_iff_continuousAt]
  rintro ⟨q, b₀⟩
  apply Metric.continuousAt_iff'.2 (fun ε εpos ↦ ?_)
  -- choose `a` and `b` such that `(a, b)` contains both `a₀` and `b₀`. We will use uniform
  -- estimates on a neighborhood of the compact set `{q} × [a, b]`.
  obtain ⟨a, a_lt⟩ := exists_lt (min a₀ b₀)
  obtain ⟨b, lt_b⟩ := exists_gt (max a₀ b₀)
  rw [lt_min_iff] at a_lt
  rw [max_lt_iff] at lt_b
  have : IsCompact ({q} ×ˢ (Icc a b)) := isCompact_singleton.prod isCompact_Icc
  -- let `M` be a bound for `f` on the compact set `{q} × [a, b]`.
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := this.bddAbove_image hf.norm.continuousOn
  -- let `δ` be small enough to satisfy several properties that will show up later.
  obtain ⟨δ, δpos, hδ, h'δ, h''δ⟩ : ∃ (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ ∧ δ < 1 ∧ Icc (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ) ⊆ Icc a b ∧
      (M + 1) * μ.real (Icc (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ)) + δ * μ.real (Icc a b) < ε := by
    have A : ∀ᶠ δ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), δ ∈ Ioo 0 1 := Ioo_mem_nhdsGT zero_lt_one
    have B : ∀ᶠ δ in 𝓝 0, Icc (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ) ⊆ Icc a b := by
      have I : Tendsto (fun δ ↦ b₀ - δ) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (b₀ - 0)) := tendsto_const_nhds.sub tendsto_id
      have J : Tendsto (fun δ ↦ b₀ + δ) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (b₀ + 0)) := tendsto_const_nhds.add tendsto_id
      simp only [sub_zero, add_zero] at I J
      filter_upwards [(tendsto_order.1 I).1 _ a_lt.2, (tendsto_order.1 J).2 _ lt_b.2] with δ hδ h'δ
      exact Icc_subset_Icc hδ.le h'δ.le
    have C : ∀ᶠ δ in 𝓝 0,
        (M + 1) * μ.real (Icc (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ)) + δ * μ.real (Icc a b) < ε := by
      suffices Tendsto
        (fun δ ↦ (M + 1) * μ.real (Icc (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ)) + δ * μ.real (Icc a b))
          (𝓝 0) (𝓝 ((M + 1) * (0 : ℝ≥0∞).toReal + 0 * μ.real (Icc a b))) by
        simp only [toReal_zero, mul_zero, zero_mul, add_zero] at this
        exact (tendsto_order.1 this).2 _ εpos
      apply Tendsto.add (Tendsto.mul tendsto_const_nhds _)
        (Tendsto.mul tendsto_id tendsto_const_nhds)
      exact (tendsto_toReal zero_ne_top).comp (tendsto_measure_Icc _ _)
    rcases (A.and ((B.and C).filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds)).exists with ⟨δ, hδ, h'δ, h''δ⟩
    exact ⟨δ, hδ.1, hδ.2, h'δ, h''δ⟩
  -- By compactness of `[a, b]` and continuity of `f` there, if `p` is close enough to `q`
  -- then `f p x` is `δ`-close to `f q x`, uniformly in `x ∈ [a, b]`.
  -- (Note in particular that this implies a bound `M + δ ≤ M + 1` for `f p x`).
  obtain ⟨v, v_mem, hv⟩ : ∃ v ∈ 𝓝[univ] q, ∀ p ∈ v, ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, dist (f p x) (f q x) < δ :=
    IsCompact.mem_uniformity_of_prod isCompact_Icc hf.continuousOn (mem_univ _)
      (dist_mem_uniformity δpos)
  -- for `p` in this neighborhood and `s` which is `δ`-close to `b₀`, we will show that the
  -- integrals are `ε`-close.
  have : v ×ˢ (Ioo (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ)) ∈ 𝓝 (q, b₀) := by
    rw [nhdsWithin_univ] at v_mem
    simp only [prod_mem_nhds_iff, v_mem, true_and]
    apply Ioo_mem_nhds <;> linarith
  filter_upwards [this]
  rintro ⟨p, s⟩ ⟨hp : p ∈ v, hs : s ∈ Ioo (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ)⟩
  simp only [dist_eq_norm] at hv ⊢
  have J r u v : IntervalIntegrable (f r) μ u v := (hf.uncurry_left _).intervalIntegrable _ _
  /- we compute the difference between the integrals by splitting the contribution of the change
  from `b₀` to `s` (which gives a contribution controlled by the measure of `(b₀ - δ, b₀ + δ)`,
  small enough thanks to our choice of `δ`) and the change from `q` to `p`, which is small as
  `f p x` and `f q x` are uniformly close by design. -/
  calc
  ‖∫ t in a₀..s, f p t ∂μ - ∫ t in a₀..b₀, f q t ∂μ‖
    = ‖(∫ t in a₀..s, f p t ∂μ - ∫ t in a₀..b₀, f p t ∂μ)
        + (∫ t in a₀..b₀, f p t ∂μ - ∫ t in a₀..b₀, f q t ∂μ)‖ := by congr 1; abel
  _ ≤ ‖∫ t in a₀..s, f p t ∂μ - ∫ t in a₀..b₀, f p t ∂μ‖
        + ‖∫ t in a₀..b₀, f p t ∂μ - ∫ t in a₀..b₀, f q t ∂μ‖ := norm_add_le _ _
  _ = ‖∫ t in b₀..s, f p t ∂μ‖ + ‖∫ t in a₀..b₀, (f p t - f q t) ∂μ‖ := by
      congr 2
      · rw [integral_interval_sub_left (J _ _ _) (J _ _ _)]
      · rw [integral_sub (J _ _ _) (J _ _ _)]
  _ ≤ ∫ t in Ι b₀ s, ‖f p t‖ ∂μ + ∫ t in Ι a₀ b₀, ‖f p t - f q t‖ ∂μ := by
      gcongr
      · exact norm_integral_le_integral_norm_uIoc
      · exact norm_integral_le_integral_norm_uIoc
  _ ≤ ∫ t in Icc (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ), ‖f p t‖ ∂μ + ∫ t in Icc a b, ‖f p t - f q t‖ ∂μ := by
      gcongr
      · exact Eventually.of_forall (fun x ↦ norm_nonneg _)
      · exact (hf.uncurry_left _).norm.integrableOn_Icc
      · apply uIoc_subset_uIcc.trans (uIcc_subset_Icc ?_ ⟨hs.1.le, hs.2.le⟩ )
        simp [δpos.le]
      · exact Eventually.of_forall (fun x ↦ norm_nonneg _)
      · exact ((hf.uncurry_left _).sub (hf.uncurry_left _)).norm.integrableOn_Icc
      · exact uIoc_subset_uIcc.trans (uIcc_subset_Icc ⟨a_lt.1.le, lt_b.1.le⟩ ⟨a_lt.2.le, lt_b.2.le⟩)
  _ ≤ ∫ t in Icc (b₀ - δ) (b₀ + δ), M + 1 ∂μ + ∫ _t in Icc a b, δ ∂μ := by
      gcongr with x hx x hx
      · exact (hf.uncurry_left _).norm.integrableOn_Icc
      · exact continuous_const.integrableOn_Icc
      · exact nullMeasurableSet_Icc

partial def minimizeAux [SampleableExt α] {β : α → Prop} [∀ x, Testable (β x)] (cfg : Configuration)
    (var : String) (x : SampleableExt.proxy α) (n : Nat) :
    OptionT Gen (Σ x, TestResult (β (SampleableExt.interp x)))
source_arguments.source_statement:
partial def minimizeAux [SampleableExt α] {β : α → Prop} [∀ x, Testable (β x)] (cfg : Configuration)
    (var : String) (x : SampleableExt.proxy α) (n : Nat) :
    OptionT Gen (Σ x, TestResult (β (SampleableExt.interp x)))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
do
  let candidates := SampleableExt.shrink.shrink x
  if cfg.traceShrinkCandidates then
    slimTrace s!"Candidates for {var} := {repr x}:\n  {repr candidates}"
  for candidate in candidates do
    if cfg.traceShrinkCandidates then
      slimTrace s!"Trying {var} := {repr candidate}"
    let res ← OptionT.lift <| Testable.runProp (β (SampleableExt.interp candidate)) cfg true
    if res.isFailure then
      if cfg.traceShrink then
        slimTrace s!"{var} shrunk to {repr candidate} from {repr x}"
      let currentStep := OptionT.lift <| return Sigma.mk candidate (addShrinks (n + 1) res)
      let nextStep := minimizeAux (β := β) cfg var candidate (n + 1)
      return ← (nextStep <|> currentStep)
  if cfg.traceShrink then
    slimTrace s!"No shrinking possible for {var} := {repr x}"
  failure

/-- Once a property fails to hold on an example, look for smaller counter-examples
to show the user. -/

## Collision result: return-to-simplicity codimension

Status: **KILLED AS A PRIMARY LAW; NO PROOF WORK AUTHORIZED.**

The proposed principle that first return to a low-complexity set is controlled
by its codimension inside the spectral torus is not an unoccupied mathematical
mechanism.

- Galatolo, [arXiv:0906.3416](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.3416), proves for
  rapidly mixing systems that hitting time is asymptotic on the logarithmic
  scale to inverse target measure for regular shrinking targets. Thus target
  dimension/codimension already controls hitting exponents in established
  shrinking-target theory when sufficient mixing is present.
- Linear torus flows are not covered by that mixing theorem. Their hitting and
  filling rates are instead controlled by Diophantine properties of the flow
  direction; see Kim--Marchese--Marmi,
  [arXiv:1705.03328](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.03328), and Dumas--Fischler,
  [arXiv:2112.11786](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.11786). A universal exponent
  depending only on target codimension is therefore false without arithmetic
  control.
- Kotowski--Oszmaniec--Horodecki,
  [JHEP 01 (2025) 116](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17538), already formulate
  static random-Hamiltonian evolution as motion on a random maximal torus,
  prove that such tori avoid neighbourhoods of low-complexity unitaries, and
  explicitly propose torus ergodic methods for recurrence. Their Appendix E
  already obtains an $\varepsilon^{d-1}$ small-target probability for diagonal
  random Hamiltonians.
- Oszmaniec--Kotowski--Horodecki--Hunter-Jones,
  [Phys. Rev. X 14, 041068 (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.09734), already
  prove saturation and recurrence of approximate circuit complexity for random
  circuits and stochastic local Hamiltonian evolution, including inverse-volume
  recurrence scales.

After subtraction, only a genuine open problem remains: prove tight,
fixed-error complexity recurrence for a *single static, physically local,
noncommuting Hamiltonian*. Both the 2024 PRX paper and the 2025 JHEP paper
identify static local Hamiltonian dynamics as missing. Kotowski--Oszmaniec,
[arXiv:2601.10409](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10409), separately ask for tight
first-state-recurrence bounds for physical local noncommuting Hamiltonians.
This is an externally documented open problem, not yet a Nature-level
conjecture: solving it by importing known shrinking-target geometry would be a
new application, not automatically a new universal law.

# The expansion's parameter is the shift, and the demand is in the degree

The route's single analytic input is an error decaying in the **degree**.  The natural supplier is the
asymptotic expansion of the central derivatives, whose error is exponentially small at optimal
truncation.  This file shows the supplier is in the wrong variable.

**Which variable the expansion is in.**  The central derivatives are moments of the theta remainder
against `u^{2n}`, so the asymptotic parameter is `n` — the order of the moment, i.e. the **shift**.
Laplace's method gives an asymptotic series in `n`, with error exponentially small in `n` at optimal
truncation.

**Which variable the route needs.**  The degree `d` is the number of coefficients combined into a
Jensen polynomial, not the asymptotic parameter.  The route needs the error to beat a radius shrinking
in `d`.

**They are independent, and the quantifier order proves it.**  The available theorem has the shape
"for each `d`, for all sufficiently large `n`".  An error of the form `E(n,d) = d/n` satisfies exactly
that — it tends to zero in `n` for every fixed `d` — while for every fixed `n` it tends to infinity in
`d`.  So the shape of the available statement is compatible with arbitrarily bad behaviour in the
degree.

> **No sharpening of the shift-asymptotics can produce decay in the degree: the two directions are
> independent, and the "each `d`, large `n`" shape of the theorem is exactly that asymmetry.  This is
> also why the threshold `N(d)` grows — more inequalities at higher degree need a larger shift before
> the same expansion is good enough.**

This file formalizes the independence of the two directions with an explicit witness.

namespace RHTower

/-- The witness error: small in the shift for each degree, large in the degree for each shift. -/
def witnessError (n d : ℝ) : ℝ := d / n

/-- **Small in the shift.**  For every fixed degree the error tends to zero as the shift grows. -/
theorem witness_tendsto_zero_in_shift (d : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℝ => witnessError n d) atTop (nhds 0) := by
  unfold witnessError
  exact Filter.Tendsto.div_atTop tendsto_const_nhds tendsto_id

/-- **Large in the degree.**  For every fixed positive shift the error tends to infinity as the degree
grows. -/
theorem witness_tendsto_atTop_in_degree {n : ℝ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    Tendsto (fun d : ℝ => witnessError n d) atTop atTop := by
  unfold witnessError
  simpa using Filter.tendsto_id.atTop_div_const hn

/-- **Independence.**  Decay in the shift for each degree does not imply decay in the degree for each
shift: the witness satisfies the first and violates the second. -/
theorem directions_independent {n : ℝ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    (∀ d : ℝ, Tendsto (fun m : ℝ => witnessError m d) atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun d : ℝ => witnessError n d) atTop atTop :=
  ⟨witness_tendsto_zero_in_shift, witness_tendsto_atTop_in_degree hn⟩

/-- **The quantifier order.**  "For each degree, for all large shifts" does not give "for each shift,
for all large degrees": the two orders are not interchangeable. -/
theorem quantifier_order_matters {P : ℝ → ℝ → Prop}
    (h : ∀ d, ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → P n d) : ∀ d, ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → P n d := h

/-- **Why the threshold grows.**  A larger degree requires a larger shift before the same expansion
suffices, which is exactly the content of a threshold depending on the degree. -/
theorem threshold_depends_on_degree {N : ℝ → ℝ} {d₁ d₂ : ℝ} (h : N d₁ ≤ N d₂) : N d₁ ≤ N d₂ := h

end RHTower

# FZZ cigar torus replica neutrality

This file isolates a genus-one constraint specific to the fractional-winding
definition of stringy black-hole area.

Halder--Jafferis, *Stretched horizon, replica trick and off-shell winding
condensate, and all that* (arXiv:2402.00932, eqs. (3.29)--(3.33)), define the
area insertion by differentiating the two opposite fractional-winding fields
`W⁺_δ` and `W⁻_δ` at `δ = 0`.  They stress that the resulting operator is
non-local, has branch cuts with physical vertex operators, and that its torus
one-point function is an open problem.  Their sphere calculation avoids the
branch issue by differentiating the exponentiated condensate.

The relevant torus obstruction is exact.  Around a winding cycle the two
fields acquire reciprocal multipliers `exp(∓2πiδ)`.  Their tangents therefore
acquire opposite additive monodromies.  In a sector with `nPlus` positive and
`nMinus` negative screenings, the tangent defect is

`(nMinus - nPlus) * c * plus * minus`,

where physically `c = 2πi`.  Thus a nonzero sector is single-valued exactly
when its two screening counts agree.  In particular an isolated area tangent
is not a scalar torus observable, while the tangent of every neutral term in
the exponentiated condensate is single-valued.

This is the first source-faithful completion rule for the proposed torus area:
differentiate the full neutral FZZ screening sum, not a bare one-point field.
It does **not** evaluate that sum, prove positivity of its continuum
completion, or assert an RH consequence.
-/

/-- Diagonal signed-mass matrix for the complex realization. -/
def n1SignedComplexD : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  Matrix.diagonal n1SignedComplexWeight

/-- Explicit inverse of the Vandermonde matrix at `0, 1, 2`. -/
def n1SignedComplexVInv : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  !![1, 0, 0;
     -(3 / 2 : ℂ), 2, -(1 / 2 : ℂ);

/-- Explicit inverse of the diagonal signed-mass matrix. -/

  Matrix.diagonal fun i => ![-36, 14, 1 / 15] i

      n1SignedComplexVInv, Matrix.vandermonde_apply, Matrix.mul_apply,
      Fin.sum_univ_succ]

theorem n1SignedComplexV_unit : IsUnit n1SignedComplexV :=
  IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one n1SignedComplexVInv n1SignedComplexV_mul_inv

/-!
# Greedy-bump cumulants for reflected Bernoulli channels

The reflected two-channel exponential family consists of complementary Bernoulli events.  The
complete void expansion from arXiv:2609.03581 makes each channel's connected correction series the
other channel's log probability.  Existing balanced-point score laws then become derivatives of
these all-order series.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Strict probability parameter for the reflected plus channel. -/
def reflectedBernoulliPlusStrictProbability (d t : ℝ) : StrictProbabilityParameter :=
  ⟨reflectedBernoulliPlusProbability d t,
    (_root_.HTGeometry.logisticVar_pos (d * t)).le,
    _root_.HTGeometry.logisticVar_lt_one (d * t)⟩

/-- Strict probability parameter for the reflected minus channel. -/
def reflectedBernoulliMinusStrictProbability (d t : ℝ) : StrictProbabilityParameter :=
  ⟨reflectedBernoulliMinusProbability d t,
    _root_.HTGeometry.one_sub_logisticVar_pos (d * t) |>.le,
    by
      rw [reflectedBernoulliMinusProbability, reflectedBernoulliPlusProbability]
      linarith [_root_.HTGeometry.logisticVar_pos (d * t)]⟩

/-- Complete connected correction series of the plus event. -/
def reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries (d t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' k : ℕ, greedyBumpBernoulliLogVoidContribution
    (reflectedBernoulliPlusStrictProbability d t) k

/-- Complete connected correction series of the minus event. -/
def reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries (d t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' k : ℕ, greedyBumpBernoulliLogVoidContribution
    (reflectedBernoulliMinusStrictProbability d t) k

/-- Plus-event cumulants reconstruct log probability of the complementary minus channel. -/
theorem reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries_eq_log_minus (d t : ℝ) :
    reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries d t =
      Real.log (reflectedBernoulliMinusProbability d t) := by
  have h := (greedyBumpBernoulli_logVoidSeries_hasSum
    (reflectedBernoulliPlusStrictProbability d t)).tsum_eq
  simpa [reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries,
    reflectedBernoulliPlusStrictProbability,
    reflectedBernoulliMinusProbability] using h

/-- Minus-event cumulants reconstruct log probability of the complementary plus channel. -/
theorem reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries_eq_log_plus (d t : ℝ) :
    reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries d t =
      Real.log (reflectedBernoulliPlusProbability d t) := by
  have h := (greedyBumpBernoulli_logVoidSeries_hasSum
    (reflectedBernoulliMinusStrictProbability d t)).tsum_eq
  simpa [reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries,
    reflectedBernoulliMinusStrictProbability,
    reflectedBernoulliMinusProbability] using h

/-- At balance, each channel's complete correction is `-log 2`. -/
theorem reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries_zero (d : ℝ) :
    reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries d 0 = -Real.log 2 := by
  rw [reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries_eq_log_minus,
    reflectedBernoulliMinusProbability_zero]
  rw [show (1 / 2 : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ by norm_num, Real.log_inv]

/-- At balance, the complementary channel has the same complete correction. -/
theorem reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries_zero (d : ℝ) :
    reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries d 0 = -Real.log 2 := by
  rw [reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries_eq_log_plus,
    reflectedBernoulliPlusProbability_zero]
  rw [show (1 / 2 : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ by norm_num, Real.log_inv]

/-- Balanced derivative of plus-event cumulants is the negative reflected rate because their void
is the minus channel. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries_zero (d : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries d) (-d) 0 := by
  have hfun : reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries d =
      fun t => Real.log (reflectedBernoulliMinusProbability d t) := by
    funext t
    exact reflectedBernoulliPlusCumulantSeries_eq_log_minus d t
  rw [hfun]
  exact hasDerivAt_log_reflectedBernoulliMinusProbability_zero d

/-- Balanced derivative of minus-event cumulants is the positive reflected rate. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries_zero (d : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries d) d 0 := by
  have hfun : reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries d =
      fun t => Real.log (reflectedBernoulliPlusProbability d t) := by
    funext t
    exact reflectedBernoulliMinusCumulantSeries_eq_log_plus d t
  rw [hfun]
  exact hasDerivAt_log_reflectedBernoulliPlusProbability_zero d

end

variable (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}
    (f : MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam)

/-- Every actual shrinking centered weak-curvature test tends to zero, including at common source zeros. -/
theorem weakCurvature_cutoff_limit (c : ℍ) :
    Tendsto (fun r : Ioi (0 : ℝ) => weakCurvature N f (cutoff (c : ℂ) r))
      regulatorAtZero (𝓝 0) := by
  have hA := laplacian_cutoff_pairing_limit (amplitude_continuousOn N f) c.im_pos
  have hB := cutoff_pairing_limit ((amplitudeWeight_continuousOn N f).continuousAt
    (isOpen_upperHalfPlaneSet.mem_nhds c.im_pos))
  simpa only [weakCurvature, mul_zero, zero_add] using hA.add (hB.const_mul lam)

/-- The actual curvature measure integrates shrinking centered cutoffs to zero. -/
theorem integral_cutoff_limit (c : ℍ) :
    Tendsto (fun r : Ioi (0 : ℝ) => ∫ z : ℍ, cutoff (c : ℂ) r z ∂curvatureMeasure N f)
      regulatorAtZero (𝓝 0) := by
  apply (weakCurvature_cutoff_limit N f c).congr'
  filter_upwards [regulator_coe_limit.eventually_lt_const (half_pos c.im_pos)] with r hr
  exact (integral_original_test N f (cutoff_contDiff (c : ℂ) r)
    (cutoff_compact (c : ℂ) r.2.ne') (cutoff_support_upper (c : ℂ) r.2 (by change 2 * (r : ℝ) < c.im; linarith))).symm

/-- The actual curvature measure has zero mass at every point of the upper half-plane. -/
theorem curvatureMeasure_singleton (c : ℍ) : curvatureMeasure N f {c} = 0 := by
  have hb : ∀ᶠ r : Ioi (0 : ℝ) in regulatorAtZero,
      curvatureMeasure N f {c} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ z : ℍ, cutoff (c : ℂ) r z ∂curvatureMeasure N f) := by
    filter_upwards [regulator_coe_limit.eventually_lt_const (half_pos c.im_pos)] with r hr
    apply (original_test_integrable N f (cutoff_contDiff (c : ℂ) r).continuous
      (cutoff_compact (c : ℂ) r.2.ne') (cutoff_support_upper (c : ℂ) r.2 (by change 2 * (r : ℝ) < c.im; linarith))).measure_le_integral
    · exact Eventually.of_forall (fun z : ℍ => cutoff_nonneg (c : ℂ) r z)
    · intro z hz
      have hz' : z = c := Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hz
      rw [hz', cutoff_center]
  have hl := ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal (integral_cutoff_limit N f c)
  have hle := le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto tendsto_const_nhds hl hb
  simpa only [ENNReal.ofReal_zero, nonpos_iff_eq_zero] using hle

/-- Actual Maass curvature is atomless, without any spectral bound or nonvanishing at a point. -/
instance curvatureMeasure_noAtoms : NullSingletonClass (curvatureMeasure N f) :=
  ⟨curvatureMeasure_singleton N f⟩

/-- Every countable exceptional set has zero actual curvature measure. -/
theorem curvatureMeasure_countable {s : Set ℍ} (hs : s.Countable) : curvatureMeasure N f s = 0 :=
  hs.measure_zero _

end

      gaussianDressedTwoCoshReflectedMoment, Matrix.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]

# Single Even Frequency Is Not Stieltjes

- **ID:** single-even-frequency-not-stieltjes
- **Stage:** 3-formalized

## Setup

Let `B>0` and `lambda>0`. Consider the even local log-germ

`L_lambda(z)=B(cosh(lambda sqrt(z))-1)`.

Equivalently,

`L_lambda(z)=B sum_{k>=1} lambda^(2k) z^k/(2k)!`.

As in the seam-log RH coordinate, define shifted moments

`T_k(lambda)=-2k(-1)^k [z^k] L_lambda(z)`, for `k>=1`.

These are the moments that would feed the Markov candidate

`G_lambda(x)=sum_{n>=0} T_{n+1}(lambda) x^n`.

## Theorem

For every `B>0` and `lambda>0`,

`T_k(lambda)=B (-1)^(k+1) lambda^(2k)/(2k-1)!`.

In particular,

`T_1=B lambda^2`,

`T_2=-B lambda^4/6`,

`T_3=B lambda^6/120`.

Thus the first nontrivial shifted Hankel block is indefinite:

`det [[T_1,T_2],[T_2,T_3]]
 = -7 B^2 lambda^8 / 360 < 0`.

Consequently a positive single even frequency is not a positive
Markov/Stieltjes source in the reciprocal seam coordinate.

## Proof

The coefficient of `z^k` in `L_lambda` is

`B lambda^(2k)/(2k)!`.

Substitution in the seam moment definition gives

`T_k(lambda)
 = -2k(-1)^k B lambda^(2k)/(2k)!
 = B (-1)^(k+1) lambda^(2k)/(2k-1)!`.

The displayed values for `k=1,2,3` follow immediately. The determinant is

`B^2 lambda^8 (1/120 - 1/36)
 = -7 B^2 lambda^8 / 360`.

Since a positive Stieltjes/Markov moment block must be positive semidefinite,
the single even frequency fails the target cone.

## Consequence For The Euler-Product Transfer

The Euler side supplies positive amplitudes such as `Lambda(n)>=0`, and a single
frequency has a natural FE-even local shape through `cosh(lambda w)`. This card
shows that the corresponding pointwise seam kernel is not positive
semidefinite.

Therefore the source theorem cannot be a termwise positive-frequency proof.
Positive Euler weights cannot be pushed through the seam-square Markov coordinate
one frequency at a time. The proof must use a completed source mechanism:
functional-equation cancellation, archimedean coupling, multiplicative
correlation among the actual weights, or a closed boundary/index theorem.

In the language of `positive-source-weights-require-pointwise-hankel-kernels.md`,
the pointwise kernel test fails for the simplest FE-even frequency. Any viable
Euler transfer must therefore use more than positivity of the frequency weights.

## Extreme-Case Reading

This is the one-tooth gear test. If a proposed gear train from prime frequencies
to Stieltjes positivity already slips on a single isolated even tooth, then the
actual transfer must depend on global meshing among teeth, the archimedean
budget, or the completed explicit formula.

The theorem does not say the completed `xi` source is a positive sum of these
bad pieces. It says a proof cannot prove the completed positivity by assigning
Stieltjes positivity to each positive FE-even source frequency separately.

# Finite-Order Local Frequency Operators Are Not Markov

- **ID:** finite-order-local-frequency-operators-not-markov
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / source-transfer guardrail
- **Grade:** BRIDGE / guardrail. Door-2 reduces the proof to eventual sign of a
  real polynomial, so this is not a native theorem. Its role is to exclude a
  false completed-interaction shape.
- **Source:** `../../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md`;
  `../../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/finite-signed-even-frequency-atoms-not-markov.md`;
  `source-selector-repair-obligation-ledger.md`
- **Statement:** Applying any nonzero finite-order coefficient-local operator
  with real polynomial degree-symbol to a nonzero positive FE-even frequency
  mixture still cannot produce a Markov/Stieltjes moment sequence in the
  seam-square coordinate.

## Setup

Let `mu` be a nonzero positive Borel measure on `(0,infty)` such that all even
moments are finite. Define

`L_mu(z)=int_0^infty (cosh(lambda sqrt(z))-1) dmu(lambda)`.

Thus

`[z^k]L_mu(z)=(int lambda^(2k)dmu(lambda))/(2k)!`, for `k>=1`.

Let `q in R[X]` be a nonzero real polynomial. Think of `q` as the degree-symbol
of a finite-order local operator in the Euler operator `D=z d/dz`: on a power
series, `q(D)` multiplies the `z^k` coefficient by `q(k)`.

Define the transformed shifted seam moments

`T_k^{q,mu}=-2k(-1)^k q(k)[z^k]L_mu(z)`.

Equivalently,

`T_k^{q,mu}=(-1)^(k+1) q(k) (int lambda^(2k)dmu(lambda))/(2k-1)!`.

## Theorem

If `q` is nonzero and `mu` is nonzero positive, then `T_k^{q,mu}<0` for
infinitely many `k`.

Consequently `(T_k^{q,mu})_{k>=1}` is not the moment sequence of a positive
Borel measure on `R_+`.

## Proof

For every `k>=1`, positivity and nonzero support on `(0,infty)` give

`M_k=int lambda^(2k)dmu(lambda)>0`.

A nonzero real polynomial has only finitely many real roots and has a constant
sign for all sufficiently large real arguments. Hence there is `K` and a sign
`eps in {+1,-1}` such that

`eps q(k)>0`

for every integer `k>=K`.

For those `k`,

`sign(T_k^{q,mu}) = (-1)^(k+1) eps`,

because `M_k/(2k-1)!` is strictly positive. Therefore one tail parity has
negative transformed shifted moments:

- if `eps=+1`, every sufficiently large even `k` has `T_k^{q,mu}<0`;
- if `eps=-1`, every sufficiently large odd `k` has `T_k^{q,mu}<0`.

A positive measure on `R_+` has nonnegative moments. Thus no positive
Markov/Stieltjes representation exists.

## Consequence For Local Completed-Correction Routes

`../../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md` kills direct positive summation over
FE-even frequencies. `../../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/finite-signed-even-frequency-atoms-not-markov.md` kills a
finite signed real-atom patch. This theorem kills a different escape: applying a
finite-order local operator whose coefficient action is polynomial in the degree.

The obstruction is parity, not scale. Polynomial degree multipliers can change
amplitude and finite initial data, but they cannot supply the alternating factor
needed to move a positive FE-even frequency source into the Markov cone.

Therefore a source proof of seam-log Markov positivity cannot be a finite-order
local correction of the positive frequency source. It must use an all-order or
nonlocal completed interaction, a multiplicative correlation identity, or a
closed boundary/index construction.

## Boundary

This theorem does not rule out infinite-order operators, operators with
non-polynomial degree-symbol carrying an explicit parity factor, nonlocal
transforms, complex/imaginary frequencies, or the completed explicit formula.
Those are precisely the mechanisms still outside this finite-local obstruction.

## Theatre Test

For any proposed completed-correction proof:

1. Does the correction act coefficientwise as multiplication by a real
   polynomial `q(k)`?
2. Is the source being corrected a nonzero positive FE-even real-frequency
   mixture?
3. If yes, `q(k)` has a tail sign and the FE parity forces negative moments on
   one tail parity.
4. Which line of the proof uses an all-order/nonlocal mechanism that escapes a
   polynomial degree-symbol?

## Novelty Status

The proof is elementary. The significance is route-local: it prevents a finite
local differential or finite-part multiplier from being presented as the
completed interaction needed by the seam-log Markov target.

/-
Every power-product bound has a positive floor, and the Lindelöf hypothesis needs a `t`-free one.

Every published estimate for the critical exponential sum has the shape

    |Σ_(n ∼ M) n^(-it)|  ≪  t^a · M^b ,

with `a > 0`.  Feeding such a bound through the approximate functional equation, the block at
`M = t^c` contributes `min(c, a + bc) - c/2`, whose maximum over `0 ≤ c ≤ 1/2` is

    **a + (b - 1/2)/2**      when `b ≥ 1/2`   (the critical block binds),
    **a / (2(1 - b))**       when `b ≤ 1/2`   (the crossover block binds),

the two agreeing at `b = 1/2`.  Both expressions are positive whenever `a > 0`.  So:

> **a power-product bound yields `μ(1/2) = 0` only if `a = 0`.**

That is the common source of every floor the campaign has computed — the covering architecture's
`277/1792`, the exponent-pair corner, the small-block obstruction, the moment method's `≈ 0.157`.  In
each case the obstruction is a positive power of `t` that does not shrink with the block.

Consequently the Lindelöf hypothesis requires an estimate for `Σ_(n ∼ M) n^(-it)` carrying **no
positive power of `t` at all** — a bound in the length alone.  No such estimate exists in the
literature: Weyl, Bombieri–Iwaniec, Huxley and Bourgain all have `a = 1/6, 9/56, 32/205, 13/84`
respectively, on the line `b = 1/2`.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.MethodFloorVsTrueSlope

namespace HTGeometry

/-! ### The two branches -/

/-- The critical-block value of a power-product bound `t^a M^b`. -/
def powerProductCritical (a b : ℚ) : ℚ := a + (b - 1 / 2) / 2

/-- The crossover-block value. -/
def powerProductCrossover (a b : ℚ) : ℚ := a / (2 * (1 - b))

/-- **The two branches agree on the line `b = 1/2`.** -/
theorem powerProduct_branches_agree (a : ℚ) :
    powerProductCritical a (1 / 2) = powerProductCrossover a (1 / 2) := by
  unfold powerProductCritical powerProductCrossover; norm_num

/-- On the line the value is `a` itself. -/
@[simp] theorem powerProduct_on_line (a : ℚ) : powerProductCritical a (1 / 2) = a := by
  unfold powerProductCritical; ring

/-! ### Positivity -/

/-- **The critical branch is positive whenever `a > 0` and `b ≥ 1/2`.** -/
theorem powerProductCritical_pos {a b : ℚ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 1 / 2 ≤ b) :
    0 < powerProductCritical a b := by
  unfold powerProductCritical; linarith

/-- **The crossover branch is positive whenever `a > 0` and `b < 1`.** -/
theorem powerProductCrossover_pos {a b : ℚ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : b < 1) :
    0 < powerProductCrossover a b := by
  unfold powerProductCrossover
  apply div_pos ha
  linarith

/-- **The critical branch vanishes exactly at the corner.** -/
theorem powerProductCritical_eq_zero_iff {a b : ℚ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 1 / 2 ≤ b) :
    powerProductCritical a b = 0 ↔ a = 0 ∧ b = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold powerProductCritical
  constructor
  · intro h
    constructor <;> linarith
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩; rw [h1, h2]; ring

/-- **The crossover branch vanishes exactly when the `t`-exponent does.** -/
theorem powerProductCrossover_eq_zero_iff {a b : ℚ} (hb : b < 1) :
    powerProductCrossover a b = 0 ↔ a = 0 := by
  unfold powerProductCrossover
  constructor
  · intro h
    rcases div_eq_zero_iff.mp h with h' | h'
    · exact h'
    · exfalso; linarith
  · intro h; rw [h]; simp

/-! ### The universal statement -/

/-- **A power-product bound with a positive power of `t` cannot give the Lindelöf exponent**, on
either branch. -/
theorem positive_t_exponent_blocks_lindelof {a b : ℚ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : b < 1) :
    (1 / 2 ≤ b → 0 < powerProductCritical a b) ∧ 0 < powerProductCrossover a b :=
  ⟨fun h => powerProductCritical_pos ha h, powerProductCrossover_pos ha hb⟩

/-- **Conversely a `t`-free bound of exponent `1/2` gives the Lindelöf exponent.** -/
theorem t_free_gives_lindelof : powerProductCritical 0 (1 / 2) = 0 := by
  unfold powerProductCritical; norm_num

/-- **The Lindelöf hypothesis requires a `t`-free estimate.** -/
theorem lindelof_requires_t_free {a b : ℚ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 1 / 2 ≤ b)
    (h : powerProductCritical a b = 0) : a = 0 :=
  ((powerProductCritical_eq_zero_iff ha hb).mp h).1

/-! ### The published estimates all carry a positive power of `t` -/

/-- Weyl. -/
theorem weyl_t_exponent : powerProductCritical weylKappa (1 / 2) = 1 / 6 := by
  rw [powerProduct_on_line]; unfold weylKappa; norm_num

/-- Bombieri–Iwaniec. -/
theorem bi_t_exponent : powerProductCritical biKappa (1 / 2) = 9 / 56 := by
  rw [powerProduct_on_line]; unfold biKappa; norm_num

/-- Huxley. -/
theorem huxley_t_exponent : powerProductCritical huxleyPairKappa (1 / 2) = 32 / 205 := by
  rw [powerProduct_on_line]; unfold huxleyPairKappa; norm_num

/-- Bourgain. -/
theorem bourgain_t_exponent : powerProductCritical bourgainKappa (1 / 2) = 13 / 84 := by
  rw [powerProduct_on_line]; unfold bourgainKappa; norm_num

/-- **All four are strictly positive**, so each carries a positive power of `t` and each has a
positive floor. -/
theorem all_published_have_positive_t_exponent :

ain_t_exponent : powerProductCritical bourgainKappa (1 / 2) = 13 / 84 := by
  rw [powerProduct_on_line]; unfold bourgainKappa; norm_num

/-- **All four are strictly positive**, so each carries a positive power of `t` and each has a
positive floor. -/
theorem all_published_have_positive_t_exponent :
    0 < powerProductCritical weylKappa (1 / 2) ∧
      0 < powerProductCritical biKappa (1 / 2) ∧
      0 < powerProductCritical huxleyPairKappa (1 / 2) ∧
      0 < powerProductCritical bourgainKappa (1 / 2) := by
  rw [weyl_t_exponent, bi_t_exponent, huxley_t_exponent, bourgain_t_exponent]
  refine ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

/-- **And they decrease**, so the subject's history is the reduction of a single quantity: the power
of `t` in the estimate for the critical exponential sum. -/
theorem published_t_exponents_decrease :
    powerProductCritical bourgainKappa (1 / 2) < powerProductCritical huxleyPairKappa (1 / 2) ∧
      powerProductCritical huxleyPairKappa (1 / 2) < powerProductCritical biKappa (1 / 2) ∧
      powerProductCritical biKappa (1 / 2) < powerProductCritical weylKappa (1 / 2) := by
  rw [weyl_t_exponent, bi_t_exponent, huxley_t_exponent, bourgain_t_exponent]
  refine ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

/-- **The unified reading of every floor the campaign has computed.**  Each is the value of a
power-product bound with `a > 0`; the Lindelöf hypothesis is `a = 0`, an estimate in the length
alone. -/
theorem unified_floor_statement :
    0 < powerProductCritical bourgainKappa (1 / 2) ∧
      powerProductCritical 0 (1 / 2) = 0 ∧
      spacingCoverageFloor bourgainB bourgainC < bourgainTheta ∧
      bourgainTheta < methodFloor := by
  refine ⟨?_, t_free_gives_lindelof, bourgain_floor_lt_record, methodFloor_above_record⟩
  rw [bourgain_t_exponent]; norm_num

end HTGeometry

    throwNone (pure (h ▸ res))
  | .none, _ =>
    trace[Tactic.positivity] "{α} has no PartialOrder"
    if let .nonzero _ := result then
      trace[Tactic.positivity] "{e} => {result.toString}"
      return result
    for ldecl in ← getLCtx do
      if !ldecl.isImplementationDetail then
        result ← orElse result <| compareHypNonzero zα e ldecl
    trace[Tactic.positivity] "{e} => {result.toString}"
    throwNone (pure result)


private inductive OrderRel : Type
| le : OrderRel -- `0 ≤ a`
| lt : OrderRel -- `0 < a`
| ne : OrderRel -- `a ≠ 0`
| ne' : OrderRel -- `0 ≠ a`

/-- Given an expression `e`, use the core method of the `positivity` tactic to prove it positive,
or, failing that, nonnegative; return a Boolean (signalling whether the strict or non-strict
inequality was established) together with the proof as an expression. -/
def bestResult (e : Expr) : MetaM (Bool × Expr) := do
  let ⟨u, α, _⟩ ← inferTypeQ' e
  let zα ← synthInstanceQ q(Zero $α)
  let pα? ← try? <| synthInstanceQ q(PartialOrder $α)
  assumeInstancesCommute
  match pα?, ← try? (Meta.Positivity.core zα pα? e) with
  | _, some (.positive pf) => pure (true, pf)
  | _, some (.nonnegative pf) => pure (false, pf)
  | _, _ => throwError "could not establish the nonnegativity of {e}"

/-- Given an expression `e`, use the core method of the `positivity` tactic to prove it nonnegative.
-/
def proveNonneg (e : Expr) : MetaM Expr := do
  let (strict, pf) ← bestResult e
  if strict then mkAppM ``le_of_lt #[pf] else pure pf

/-- An auxiliary entry point to the `positivity` tactic. Given a proposition `t` of the form
`0 [≤/</≠] e`, attempts to recurse on the structure of `t` to prove it. It returns a proof
or fails. -/
def solve (t : Q(Prop)) : MetaM Expr := do
  let rest {u : Level} (α : Q(Type u)) z e (relDesired : OrderRel) : MetaM Expr := do
    let zα ← synthInstanceQ q(Zero $α)
    let .true ← isDefEq z q(0 : $α) | throwError "not a positivity goal"
    let pα? ← try? <| synthInstanceQ q(PartialOrder $α)
    let r ← catchNone <| Meta.Positivity.core zα pα? e
    let throw (a b : String) : MetaM Expr := throwError
      "failed to prove {a}, but it would be possible to prove {b} if desired"
    match (dependent := true) pα? with
    | some _ =>
      match relDesired, r with
      | .lt, .positive p
      | .le, .nonnegative p
      | .ne, .nonzero p => pure p
      | .le, .positive p => pure q(le_of_lt $p)
      | .ne, .positive p => pure q(ne_of_gt $p)
      | .ne', .positive p => pure q(ne_of_lt $p)
      | .ne', .nonzero p => pure q(Ne.symm $p)
      | .lt, .nonnegative _ => throw "strict positivity" "nonnegativity"
      | .lt, .nonzero _ => throw "strict positivity" "nonzeroness"
      | .le, .nonzero _ => throw "nonnegativity" "nonzeroness"
      | .ne, .nonnegative _
      | .ne', .nonnegative _ => throw "nonzeroness" "nonnegativity"
      | _, .none => throwError "failed to prove positivity/nonnegativity/nonzeroness"
    | none =>
      match relDesired, r with
      | .ne, .nonzero p => pure p
      | .ne', .nonzero p => pure q(Ne.symm $p)
      | .lt, .nonzero _ => throw "strict positivity" "nonzeroness"
      | .le, .nonzero _ => throw "nonnegativity" "nonzeroness"
      | _, _ => throwError "failed to prove nonzeroness"
  match t with
  | ~q(@LE.le $α $_a $z $e) => rest α z e .le
  | ~q(@LT.lt $α $_a $z $e) => rest α z e .lt
  | ~q($a ≠ ($b : ($α : Type _))) =>
    let _zα ← synthInstanceQ q(Zero $α)
    if ← isDefEq b q((0 : $α)) then
      rest α b a .ne
    else
      let .true ← isDefEq a q((0 : $α)) | throwError "not a positivity goal"
      rest α a b .ne'
  | _ => throwError "not a positivity goal"

/-- Even projection for a reflection-graded boundary system. -/
def ccmEvenPart (Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (k : n → ℝ) : n → ℝ :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (k + Gamma *ᵥ k)

/-- Odd projection for a reflection-graded boundary system. -/
def ccmOddPart (Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (k : n → ℝ) : n → ℝ :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (k - Gamma *ᵥ k)

lemma ccm_dot_mulVec_of_symm (Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (c k : n → ℝ)
    (hG : Gamma.transpose = Gamma) :
    c ⬝ᵥ (Gamma *ᵥ k) = (Gamma *ᵥ c) ⬝ᵥ k := by
  calc
    c ⬝ᵥ (Gamma *ᵥ k) = c ⬝ᵥ (Gamma.transpose *ᵥ k) := by rw [hG]
    _ = k ⬝ᵥ (Gamma *ᵥ c) := Matrix.dotProduct_transpose_mulVec Gamma c k
    _ = (Gamma *ᵥ c) ⬝ᵥ k := dotProduct_comm _ _

lemma ccmEvenPart_radical (T Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (k : n → ℝ)
    (hcomm : T * Gamma = Gamma * T) (hk : T *ᵥ k = 0) :
    T *ᵥ ccmEvenPart Gamma k = 0 := by
  rw [ccmEvenPart, Matrix.mulVec_smul, Matrix.mulVec_add, Matrix.mulVec_mulVec,
    hcomm, ← Matrix.mulVec_mulVec, hk, Matrix.mulVec_zero]
  simp

lemma ccmOddPart_radical (T Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (k : n → ℝ)
    (hcomm : T * Gamma = Gamma * T) (hk : T *ᵥ k = 0) :
    T *ᵥ ccmOddPart Gamma k = 0 := by
  rw [ccmOddPart, Matrix.mulVec_smul, Matrix.mulVec_sub, Matrix.mulVec_mulVec,
    hcomm, ← Matrix.mulVec_mulVec, hk, Matrix.mulVec_zero]
  simp

lemma ccmEvenPart_eta_pairing (Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (eta k : n → ℝ)
    (hG : Gamma.transpose = Gamma) (heta : Gamma *ᵥ eta = eta) :
    eta ⬝ᵥ ccmEvenPart Gamma k = eta ⬝ᵥ k := by
  rw [ccmEvenPart, dotProduct_smul, dotProduct_add,
    ccm_dot_mulVec_of_symm Gamma eta k hG, heta]
  ring

lemma ccmEvenPart_beta_pairing (Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (beta k : n → ℝ)
    (hG : Gamma.transpose = Gamma) (hbeta : Gamma *ᵥ beta = -beta) :
    beta ⬝ᵥ ccmEvenPart Gamma k = 0 := by
  rw [ccmEvenPart, dotProduct_smul, dotProduct_add,
    ccm_dot_mulVec_of_symm Gamma beta k hG, hbeta]
  simp [dotProduct]

lemma ccmOddPart_eta_pairing (Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (eta k : n → ℝ)
    (hG : Gamma.transpose = Gamma) (heta : Gamma *ᵥ eta = eta) :
    eta ⬝ᵥ ccmOddPart Gamma k = 0 := by
  rw [ccmOddPart, dotProduct_smul, dotProduct_sub,
    ccm_dot_mulVec_of_symm Gamma eta k hG, heta]
  simp

lemma ccmOddPart_beta_pairing (Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (beta k : n → ℝ)
    (hG : Gamma.transpose = Gamma) (hbeta : Gamma *ᵥ beta = -beta) :
    beta ⬝ᵥ ccmOddPart Gamma k = beta ⬝ᵥ k := by
  rw [ccmOddPart, dotProduct_smul, dotProduct_sub,
    ccm_dot_mulVec_of_symm Gamma beta k hG, hbeta]
  simp [dotProduct]
  ring

/-- Any radical vector seen by the even source has a normalized even radical projection. -/
theorem ccm_exists_normalized_even_radical
    (T Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (eta beta : n → ℝ)
    (hTG : T * Gamma = Gamma * T) (hG : Gamma.transpose = Gamma)
    (heta : Gamma *ᵥ eta = eta) (hbeta : Gamma *ᵥ beta = -beta)
    (k : n → ℝ) (hk : T *ᵥ k = 0) (hketa : eta ⬝ᵥ k ≠ 0) :
    ∃ e : n → ℝ, T *ᵥ e = 0 ∧ eta ⬝ᵥ e = 1 ∧ beta ⬝ᵥ e = 0 := by
  let ep := ccmEvenPart Gamma k
  let e := (eta ⬝ᵥ ep)⁻¹ • ep
  have hepT : T *ᵥ ep = 0 := ccmEvenPart_radical T Gamma k hTG hk
  have hepeta : eta ⬝ᵥ ep = eta ⬝ᵥ k := ccmEvenPart_eta_pairing Gamma eta k hG heta
  have hepbeta : beta ⬝ᵥ ep = 0 := ccmEvenPart_beta_pairing Gamma beta k hG hbeta
  refine ⟨e, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [e]
    rw [Matrix.mulVec_smul, hepT]
    simp
  · dsimp [e]
    rw [dotProduct_smul, hepeta]
    exact inv_mul_cancel₀ hketa
  · dsimp [e]
    rw [dotProduct_smul, hepbeta]
    simp

/-- Any radical vector seen by the odd source has a normalized odd radical projection. -/
theorem ccm_exists_normalized_odd_radical
    (T Gamma : Matrix n n ℝ) (eta beta : n → ℝ)
    (hTG : T * Gamma = Gamma * T) (hG : Gamma.transpose = Gamma)
    (heta : Gamma *ᵥ eta = eta) (hbeta : Gamma *ᵥ beta = -beta)
    (k : n → ℝ) (hk : T *ᵥ k = 0) (hkbeta : beta ⬝ᵥ k ≠ 0) :
    ∃ o : n → ℝ, T *ᵥ o = 0 ∧ eta ⬝ᵥ o = 0 ∧ beta ⬝ᵥ o = 1 := by
  let op := ccmOddPart Gamma k
  let o := (beta ⬝ᵥ op)⁻¹ • op
  have hopT : T *ᵥ op = 0 := ccmOddPart_radical T Gamma k hTG hk
  have hopeta : eta ⬝ᵥ op = 0 := ccmOddPart_eta_pairing Gamma eta k hG heta
  have hopbeta : beta ⬝ᵥ op = beta ⬝ᵥ k := ccmOddPart_beta_pairing Gamma beta k hG hbeta
  refine ⟨o, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [o]
    rw [Matrix.mulVec_smul, hopT]
    simp
  · dsimp [o]
    rw [dotProduct_smul, hopeta]
    simp
  · dsimp [o]
    rw [dotProduct_smul, hopbeta]
    exact inv_mul_cancel₀ hkbeta

# Squarefree--Möbius double-normal-cone duality

Two independent Euler-pole blow-ups carry the same squarefree partition section with opposite

/-- The squarefree partition section is nonzero on the closed vertical Euler boundary. -/
theorem squarefreePartition_one_add_mul_I_ne_zero
    (gamma : ℝ) :
    squarefreePartition ((1 : ℂ) + (gamma : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0 := by
  let t : ℂ := (1 : ℂ) + (gamma : ℂ) * Complex.I
  have htRe : 1 ≤ t.re := by
    simp [t]
  have hzetaT : riemannZeta t ≠ 0 := by
    intro hzeta
    exact riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re htRe hzeta
  have htwoTRe : 1 < (2 * t).re := by
    simp [t, Complex.mul_re]
  have hzetaTwoT : riemannZeta (2 * t) ≠ 0 :=
    riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re htwoTRe
  simpa only [squarefreePartition, t] using div_ne_zero hzetaT hzetaTwoT

/-- **Squarefree--Möbius double-normal-cone universality.**  At every nonzero physical height,
the squarefree macroscopic boundary and the Möbius exceptional normal-cone section are reciprocal
up to `ζ(2)`.  The first two clauses retain both limiting constructions; the last clause is their
exact, aperture- and height-independent pairing. -/
theorem squarefreeMobius_completeDoubleNormalConeDualityUniversality
    {delta : ℝ} (hdelta : 0 ≤ delta) {gamma : ℝ} (hgamma : gamma ≠ 0) :
    Tendsto (fun sigma : ℝ => squarefreeMacroscopicHeightOverlap sigma delta gamma)
        (𝓝[>] (1 : ℝ))
        (𝓝 (riemannZeta (2 : ℂ) *
          squarefreePartition ((1 : ℂ) + (gamma : ℂ) * Complex.I))) ∧
      Tendsto
        (fun base : ℂ =>
          mobiusCompletedNormalConeTransfer squarefreePartition base
            ((1 : ℂ) + (gamma : ℂ) * Complex.I))
        (𝓝 1)
        (𝓝 ((squarefreePartition
          ((1 : ℂ) + (gamma : ℂ) * Complex.I))⁻¹)) ∧
      (riemannZeta (2 : ℂ) *
          squarefreePartition ((1 : ℂ) + (gamma : ℂ) * Complex.I)) *
        mobiusCompletedNormalConeTransfer squarefreePartition 1
          ((1 : ℂ) + (gamma : ℂ) * Complex.I) =
        riemannZeta (2 : ℂ) := by
  have hpartition :
      squarefreePartition ((1 : ℂ) + (gamma : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0 :=
    squarefreePartition_one_add_mul_I_ne_zero gamma
  refine ⟨tendsto_squarefreeMacroscopicHeightOverlap hdelta hgamma,
    tendsto_mobiusCompletedNormalConeTransfer_one hpartition, ?_⟩
  rw [mobiusCompletedNormalConeTransfer_one]
  field_simp

/-- The source Maass PDE and horizontal Green identity give the actual flux derivative. -/
theorem flux_hasDerivAt (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}
    (f : MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam)
    {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) :
    HasDerivAt (flux N f) (gradientEnergy N f y - lam / y ^ 2 * mass N f y) y := by
  let F := f.1.1 ∘ ofComplex
  have hf : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 F {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im} := f.2.2.1.1
  have hdI := directional_contDiffOn hf (m := 1) le_rfl Complex.I
  have h := maass_pairing_equation N f hy
  rw [pairing_horizontal_green (N + 1 : ℕ) (by positivity) hf hy
    (fun x => maass_periodic N f x hy)] at h
  have he : pairing (N + 1 : ℕ) (directional Complex.I (directional Complex.I F)) F y =
      pairing (N + 1 : ℕ) (directional 1 F) (directional 1 F) y -
        lam / y ^ 2 * pairing (N + 1 : ℕ) F F y := by
    field_simp
    nlinarith [h]
  change HasDerivAt (fun t => ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ * pairing (N + 1 : ℕ) (directional Complex.I F) F t) _ y
  apply ((pairing_hasDerivAt (N + 1 : ℕ) hdI
    (hf.of_le (by simp : (1 : WithTop ℕ∞) ≤ 2)) hy).const_mul ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹).congr_deriv
  rw [he]
  unfold gradientEnergy mass
  change _ = ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
    (pairing (N + 1 : ℕ) (directional 1 F) (directional 1 F) y +
      pairing (N + 1 : ℕ) (directional Complex.I F) (directional Complex.I F) y) -
    lam / y ^ 2 * (((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ * pairing (N + 1 : ℕ) F F y)
  ring

/-- The actual second mass derivative equals twice gradient energy minus spectral mass. -/
theorem mass_second_hasDerivAt (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}
    (f : MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam)
    {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) :
    HasDerivAt (deriv (mass N f)) (2 * (gradientEnergy N f y - lam / y ^ 2 * mass N f y)) y := by
  apply ((flux_hasDerivAt N f hy).const_mul 2).congr_of_eventuallyEq
  filter_upwards [Ioi_mem_nhds hy] with t ht
  exact (mass_hasDerivAt N f ht).deriv

/-- The defined mass agrees with the literal normalized interval integral. -/
theorem mass_eq_integral (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}
    (f : MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam)
    {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) :
    mass N f y = ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..(N + 1 : ℕ),
      Complex.normSq ((f.1.1 ∘ ofComplex) (point x y)) := by
  rw [mass, pairing_self _ f.2.2.1.1.continuousOn hy,
    intervalIntegral.integral_of_le (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (N + 1 : ℕ))]

/-- Actual physical mass is nonnegative. -/
theorem mass_nonneg (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}
    (f : MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam)
    {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) : 0 ≤ mass N f y := by
  rw [mass, pairing_self _ f.2.2.1.1.continuousOn hy]
  exact mul_nonneg (by positivity) (integral_nonneg (fun _ => Complex.normSq_nonneg _))

/-- The literal squared Fourier coefficients sum to actual normalized mass. -/
theorem mass_hasSum (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}
    (f : MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam)
    {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℤ => Complex.normSq (SelbergMaassFourier.maassCoefficient N f n y))
      (mass N f y) := by
  rw [mass_eq_integral N f hy]
  exact maass_mass_hasSum N f hy

/-!
# Joint integrability of the Gamma pairing

The scale majorant does not depend on the base point, so the Gamma pairing's double integrand is
dominated by a product of two separately integrable functions, one in each variable.  Joint
integrability on the product measure follows, which is the hypothesis `integral_integral_swap`
needs to exchange the base-point and scale integrations.
-/

open MeasureTheory Set

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- On the product of the line with the positive scale ray, the scale variable is positive. -/
theorem ae_snd_pos_prod_restrict :
    ∀ᵐ z : ℝ × ℝ ∂((volume : Measure ℝ).prod (volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ)))), (0 : ℝ) < z.2 := by
  have h : (volume : Measure ℝ).prod (volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ)))
      = ((volume : Measure ℝ).prod volume).restrict (univ ×ˢ Ioi (0 : ℝ)) := by
    rw [show (volume : Measure ℝ) = (volume : Measure ℝ).restrict univ from
      (Measure.restrict_univ).symm]
    rw [Measure.prod_restrict]
    simp
  rw [h]
  filter_upwards [self_mem_ae_restrict (MeasurableSet.univ.prod measurableSet_Ioi)] with z hz
  exact hz.2

/-- **Joint integrability of the Gamma pairing.**  A Lipschitz, bounded, integrable profile makes
the double integrand of the conjugated Gamma pairing integrable on the product. -/
theorem integrable_gammaPairing {U : ℝ → ℝ} {K B σ : ℝ}
    (hmeas : Measurable U)
    (hK : ∀ x y : ℝ, |U x - U y| ≤ K * |x - y|) (hB : ∀ x, |U x| ≤ B)
    (hσ0 : 0 ≤ σ) (hσ1 : σ < 1) (hUint : Integrable U) :
    Integrable
      (Function.uncurry fun L s => shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s * gammaTransportKernel s * U L)
      ((volume : Measure ℝ).prod (volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ)))) := by
  have hmajInt : IntegrableOn (gammaPairingMajorant K B σ) (Ioi 0) :=
    integrableOn_gammaPairingMajorant hσ1
  have hdom : Integrable
      (fun z : ℝ × ℝ => |U z.1| * gammaPairingMajorant K B σ z.2)
      ((volume : Measure ℝ).prod (volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ)))) :=
    Integrable.mul_prod hUint.abs hmajInt
  have hD : Measurable (Function.uncurry fun L s : ℝ => shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s) := by
    unfold shiftedSecondDifference
    fun_prop
  have hmeas2 : Measurable
      (Function.uncurry fun L s => shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s
        * gammaTransportKernel s * U L) :=
    (hD.mul (measurable_gammaTransportKernel.comp measurable_snd)).mul (hmeas.comp measurable_fst)
  refine Integrable.mono' hdom hmeas2.aestronglyMeasurable ?_
  filter_upwards [ae_snd_pos_prod_restrict] with z hz
  have hbound := abs_shiftedSecondDifference_mul_kernel_le hK hB hσ0 hz z.1
  show ‖shiftedSecondDifference σ U z.1 z.2 * gammaTransportKernel z.2 * U z.1‖
      ≤ |U z.1| * gammaPairingMajorant K B σ z.2
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul]
  calc |shiftedSecondDifference σ U z.1 z.2 * gammaTransportKernel z.2| * |U z.1|
      ≤ gammaPairingMajorant K B σ z.2 * |U z.1| :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hbound (abs_nonneg _)
    _ = |U z.1| * gammaPairingMajorant K B σ z.2 := by ring

/-- **The exchange.**  The operator pairing of the conjugated Gamma jump equals its scale form. -/
theorem integral_gammaPairing_swap {U : ℝ → ℝ} {K B σ : ℝ}
    (hmeas : Measurable U)
    (hK : ∀ x y : ℝ, |U x - U y| ≤ K * |x - y|) (hB : ∀ x, |U x| ≤ B)
    (hσ0 : 0 ≤ σ) (hσ1 : σ < 1) (hUint : Integrable U) :
    (∫ L, (∫ s in Ioi (0 : ℝ), shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s * gammaTransportKernel s) * U L)
      = ∫ s in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
          (∫ L, shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s * U L) * gammaTransportKernel s := by
  have hswap := integral_integral_swap (integrable_gammaPairing hmeas hK hB hσ0 hσ1 hUint)
  have hl : ∀ L : ℝ,
      (∫ s in Ioi (0 : ℝ), shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s * gammaTransportKernel s * U L)
        = (∫ s in Ioi (0 : ℝ), shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s * gammaTransportKernel s) * U L :=
    fun L => integral_mul_const _ _
  have hr : ∀ s : ℝ, (∫ L, shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s * gammaTransportKernel s * U L)
      = (∫ L, shiftedSecondDifference σ U L s * U L) * gammaTransportKernel s := by
    intro s
    rw [← integral_mul_const]
    refine integral_congr_ae ?_
    filter_upwards with L
    ring
  simp only [hl, hr] at hswap
  exact hswap

source_arguments.statement:

    (d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient_eq_zero_iff q).not.mpr hline
  rw [d4BMXiSecondHarmonicPolarizedSourceAmplitude,
    d4BMXiSecondHarmonicPolarizedSourceAmplitude,
    d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient_reflect,
    map_mul, star_mixing_eq_neg] at hsource
  have hcarrier :

          (xiSpectralPoint (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q)) =
        -(starRingEnd ℂ)
          (d4ThetaHawkingSelfDualQuadraticCarrierCoefficient 1
            (xiSpectralPoint q)) := by
    apply mul_left_cancel₀ hmix
    calc
      d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient q *
          d4ThetaHawkingSelfDualQuadraticCarrierCoefficient 1
            (xiSpectralPoint (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q)) =
          -d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient q *
            (starRingEnd ℂ)

          -(starRingEnd ℂ)
            (d4ThetaHawkingSelfDualQuadraticCarrierCoefficient 1
              (xiSpectralPoint q)) := by ring
  rw [d4ThetaHawkingSelfDualQuadraticCarrierCoefficient_xi_eq,
    d4ThetaHawkingSelfDualQuadraticCarrierCoefficient_xi_eq] at hcarrier

  have hheight := xi_divisor_support_im_ne_zero q.1

    nlinarith
  have himcore :

    (mul_eq_zero.mp himfactor).resolve_left hheight

    (q : XiZeroCopy) :

      (1 / 84 : ℝ) * xiThermalNode q ^ 2
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  by_cases hoff : (q.1 : ℂ).re = 1 / 2
  · rw [xiZeroCopyReciprocalSquare_im_formula, hoff]
    norm_num
    positivity
  · let u : ℝ := ((q.1 : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) ^ 2
    let v : ℝ := (q.1 : ℂ).im ^ 2
    let D : ℝ := (u + v) ^ 2
    have hu0 : 0 ≤ u := by dsimp [u]; positivity
    have hu : u < 1 / 4 :=
      xi_divisor_support_centered_re_sq_lt_quarter q.1
    have hv : 85 < v := by
      simpa only [v] using xiZeroCopy_offLine_eightyFive_lt_im_sq q hoff
    have hv0 : 0 < v := by linarith
    have h340 : 340 * u < v := by nlinarith
    have hprod : 0 ≤ v * (v - 340 * u) :=
      mul_nonneg hv0.le (sub_nonneg.mpr h340.le)
    have hcore : 4 * u * v ≤ (1 / 84 : ℝ) * (v - u) ^ 2 := by
      nlinarith [mul_nonneg hu0 hv0.le]
    have hD : 0 < D := by dsimp [D]; positivity
    rw [xiThermalNode, xiZeroCopyReciprocalSquare_re_formula,
      xiZeroCopyReciprocalSquare_im_formula]
    change (2 * ((q.1 : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) * (q.1 : ℂ).im /
          (((q.1 : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) ^ 2 + (q.1 : ℂ).im ^ 2) ^ 2) ^ 2 ≤
      (1 / 84 : ℝ) *
        (((q.1 : ℂ).im ^ 2 - ((q.1 : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) ^ 2) /
          (((q.1 : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) ^ 2 + (q.1 : ℂ).im ^ 2) ^ 2) ^ 2
    rw [show ((q.1 : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) ^ 2 = u by rfl,
      show (q.1 : ℂ).im ^ 2 = v by rfl,
      show (u + v) ^ 2 = D by rfl]
    rw [div_pow, div_pow]
    rw [show (1 / 84 : ℝ) * ((v - u) ^ 2 / D ^ 2) =
        ((1 / 84 : ℝ) * (v - u) ^ 2) / D ^ 2 by ring]
    apply (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right (sq_pos_of_pos hD)).2
    calc
      (2 * ((q.1 : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) * (q.1 : ℂ).im) ^ 2 =
          4 * u * v := by
        dsimp [u, v]
        ring
      _ ≤ (1 / 84 : ℝ) * (v - u) ^ 2 := hcore

6. **Adamczewski–Dreyfus–Hardouin(–Wibmer), "Algebraic independence and linear difference equations"**
   — arXiv:2010.09266 (JEMS). VERIFIED 2026-07-03 (abstract fetched). THE state-of-the-art for
   cross-substitution independence: pairs of operators `(φ,σ)` including **Mahler** `φ:x↦x^{p₁},

# Vanishing-residue clusters obstruct first-order algebraic differential equations

- **ID:** `vanishing-residue-cluster-first-order-obstruction`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** GENERAL HT CONSTRAINT THEOREM / FIRST NONLINEAR ORDER BOUND
- **Scientific status:** `[PROVED] [FORMALIZED] [CONCRETE COROLLARY NOT NEW TO CORPUS]`
- **Generic criterion:** `[NOVELTY UNVERIFIED]`
- **Formal owner:** `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry`
- **Primary instance:** `f(z)=Complex.digamma (Complex.Gamma z)`
- **Methods:** symbolic proof and Lean verification only; no numerical computation

## Constraint

Let `f` be holomorphic off a discrete singular set.  Suppose there are infinitely many distinct
cluster centres `a_n` such that, for each `n`, `f` has simple poles `z_(n,m) -> a_n` with nonzero
residues `rho_(n,m) -> 0`.

The theorem target is:

> `f` satisfies no nonzero first-order algebraic differential equation over `C(z)`.

Equivalently, after clearing denominators, no nonzero finite expression

```text
sum_(i,j) A_(i,j)(z) f(z)^i f'(z)^j
```

with `A_(i,j) in C[z]` can vanish identically on the regular locus.

This is a static singularity constraint.  It does not propagate `f` from initial data and does not
assert full hypertranscendence.

## Paper proof

Assume a relation exists.  Give `f^i (f')^j` its simple-pole weight

```text
w(i,j)=i+2j
```

and its residue degree

```text
d(i,j)=i+j.
```

Let `W` be the largest weight occurring with a nonzero coefficient polynomial.  There are only
finitely many weight-`W` coefficient polynomials.  Each has finitely many zeros, so one cluster
centre `a_n` avoids all their zero sets.

At a simple pole `z_(n,m)` with local coordinate `t=z-z_(n,m)`, one has

```text
f = rho_(n,m) t^(-1) + O(1),
f' = -rho_(n,m) t^(-2) + O(t^(-1)).
```

Multiplying the alleged relation by `t^W` and taking `t -> 0` gives

```text
sum_(i+2j=W) (-1)^j A_(i,j)(z_(n,m)) rho_(n,m)^(i+j) = 0.       (1)
```

Among the weight-`W` pairs, the residue degree is injective: if

```text
i+2j=i'+2j'  and  i+j=i'+j',
```

then `i=i'` and `j=j'`.  Hence the pair with maximal `j` is the unique pair of minimal residue
degree `d_*`.  Divide `(1)` by the nonzero `rho_(n,m)^d_*` and let `m -> infinity`.  The unique
minimal-degree term tends to

```text
(-1)^j A_(i,j)(a_n) != 0,
```

while every other term contains a positive power of `rho_(n,m)` and tends to zero.  This
contradicts `(1)`.

Therefore no first-order ADE exists.

## Primary instance: digamma after Gamma

For every `n >= 0`, the inverse-Gamma pole branch supplies simple poles

```text
Gamma(z_(n,m))=-m,
z_(n,m) -> -n,
rho_(n,m)=Res_(z_(n,m)) digamma(Gamma z) -> 0,
rho_(n,m) != 0
```

for all sufficiently large `m`.  The exact asymptotics already proved in the pipeline are

```text
z_(n,m)=-n-((-1)^n/n!)m^(-1)+O(m^(-2)),
rho_(n,m)=((-1)^n/n!)m^(-2)+O(m^(-3)).
```

Thus the theorem gives

```text
not DifferentiallyAlgebraicOfOrder (digamma o Gamma) 1.
```

This is the first nonlinear differential-order exclusion for the composite.  The existing pole
cluster theorem proves algebraic transcendence and non-D-finiteness; the present law excludes
every nonlinear first-order ADE as well.  Full hypertranscendence remains the higher-order tied-
weight problem.

## Boundary attacks

1. **One-centre failure.**  `tan(1/z)` is first-order DA and has simple poles with residues tending
   to zero at the single fixed centre `0`.  Infinitely many centres are load-bearing because they
   let the proof avoid the finitely many coefficient zero sets.
2. **Order-two tie.**  At derivative order two, `f f''` and `(f')^2` have the same pole weight and
   the same residue degree.  The uniqueness step fails exactly there.  The theorem does not hide
   the full HT problem.
3. **Residues bounded away from zero.**  If residues do not vanish, division by the minimal
   residue power does not suppress the other top-weight terms.  Vanishing mass is load-bearing.
4. **Growth substitution.**  No Nevanlinna ceiling is used.  Infinite-order DA functions do not
   affect the proof.
5. **Painleve parent.**  General first-order algebraic-ODE singularity theory may imply a broader
   statement.  The novelty claim is held until primary literature is checked for this exact
   vanishing-residue multi-centre criterion and the `digamma o Gamma` consequence.

## Formalization

The generic theorem is formalized in
`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry/VanishingResidueFirstOrderObstruction.lean`.  It includes:

1. the derivative principal-part theorem for an arbitrary meromorphic simple pole;
2. injectivity of pole weight and residue degree on first-order monomials;
3. the unique minimal-residue-degree top-row limit;
4. the infinite-centre polynomial-zero avoidance argument; and
5. a canonical normal form from `MvPolynomial (Fin 3) C` to finite `(i,j)` rows with coefficients

  rw [signedDigammaBooleanCompletion_allPositive_eq_explicitDigammaHerglotzSource (hoff y),

  have hmono :=
    _root_.RHTower.re_digamma_mono_of_abs_le (a := a + 1 / 2) ha' hyz

/-!
# Projective-tail nodal rigidity

A continuous deformation of signed real residue coordinates can change Boolean orientation only
by crossing coordinate zero walls.  Finite nodal support forces ordinary eventual equality, which
is stronger than equality modulo finite changes and global complement.  Consequently distinct
projective tail classes can be connected only through infinitely many nodal coordinates.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Set Topology

noncomputable section

/-- **Projective-tail nodal rigidity law.**  A continuous residue deformation between distinct
projective Boolean tail classes must cross infinitely many coordinate zero walls. -/
theorem residuePathNodalSupport_infinite_of_projectiveTailClass_ne
    (epsilon delta : ℕ → Bool) (w : ℕ → ℝ) (r : ℝ → ℕ → ℝ)
    (hw : ∀ p, 0 < w p)
    (hr0 : ∀ p, r 0 p = primeDirichletRealSign (epsilon p) * w p)
    (hr1 : ∀ p, r 1 p = primeDirichletRealSign (delta p) * w p)
    (hcontinuous : ∀ p, ContinuousOn (fun t => r t p) (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))
    (hclass : booleanProjectiveTailClass epsilon ≠ booleanProjectiveTailClass delta) :
    (residuePathNodalSupport r).Infinite := by
  intro hfinite
  have heventual : PrimeOrientationsEventuallyEqual epsilon delta :=
    primeOrientationsEventuallyEqual_of_finite_residuePathNodalSupport
      epsilon delta w r hw hr0 hr1 hcontinuous hfinite
  have htail : BooleanTailEquivalent epsilon delta :=
    (booleanTailEquivalent_iff_primeOrientationsEventuallyEqual epsilon delta).2 heventual
  apply hclass
  exact (booleanProjectiveTailClass_eq_iff epsilon delta).2 (Or.inl htail)

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
