/-!
# Complete signed variation and phase dispersion

Absolute summability of the selected signed Blaschke logarithmic-derivative
terms gives finite complete limits for their `l1` variation, cancellation,
and pairwise phase dispersion.  The finite-window dispersion identity passes
to these limits.

The resulting static invariants give a sharp rigidity formulation: at every
noncolliding upper observation point, RH is equivalent to simultaneous
vanishing of the complete signed resultant and complete phase dispersion.
-/

open Complex Filter MeasureTheory Metric Polynomial Set Topology
open scoped Classical ENNReal Interval Topology

namespace RiemannGaussian

noncomputable section

/-- Complete `l1` variation of the absolutely summable signed upper Blaschke
logarithmic-derivative terms. -/
def riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' rho : NontrivialZetaZero,
    ‖zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand z rho‖

/-- Complete triangle-cancellation gap of the signed upper Blaschke series. -/
def riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation z -
    ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖

/-- Complete pairwise phase dispersion of the signed upper Blaschke series. -/
def riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation z ^ 2 -
    ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖ ^ 2

/-- The complete resultant norm is bounded by complete termwise variation. -/
theorem norm_riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_le_variation
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (hxi : riemannXiSpectral z ≠ 0) :
    ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖ ≤
      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation z := by
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation
  exact norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm
    (summable_zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand hz hxi).norm

/-- Complete signed-series cancellation is nonnegative. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation_nonneg
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (hxi : riemannXiSpectral z ≠ 0) :
    0 ≤ riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation z := by
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation
  exact sub_nonneg.mpr
    (norm_riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_le_variation hz hxi)

/-- Complete phase dispersion is nonnegative. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion_nonneg
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (hxi : riemannXiSpectral z ≠ 0) :
    0 ≤ riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion z := by
  have hnorm :=
    norm_riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_le_variation hz hxi
  have hnorm0 : 0 ≤ ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖ :=
    norm_nonneg _
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion
  nlinarith

/-- Exact complete factorization of phase dispersion into cancellation times
the sum of variation and resultant norm. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion_eq_cancellation_mul_add
    (z : ℂ) :
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion z =
      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation z *
        (riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeVariation z +
          ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖) := by
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation
  ring

/-- The square of complete cancellation is bounded by complete phase
dispersion. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation_sq_le_dispersion
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (hxi : riemannXiSpectral z ≠ 0) :
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation z ^ 2 ≤
      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion z := by
  have hnorm :=
    norm_riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative_le_variation hz hxi
  have hnorm0 : 0 ≤ ‖riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivative z‖ :=
    norm_nonneg _
  unfold riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompleteLogDerivativeCancellation
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeCompletePhaseDispersion
  nlinarith

/-- A finite upper window of selected term norms is exactly the existing
finite signed-term variation. -/
theorem sum_norm_zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand_eq_variationWindow
    (z : ℂ) (T : ℝ) :
    ∑ rho ∈ spectralZetaZeroWindow T,
        ‖zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand z rho‖ =
      riemannXiUpperBlaschkeLogDerivativeVariationWindow z T := by
  unfold zetaUpperBlaschkeSelectedLogDerivativeSummand
    riemannXiUpperBlaschkeLogDerivativeVariationWindow
    spectralUpperZetaZeroWindow
  rw [Finset.sum_filter]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro rho _hrho
  by_cases hupper : rho.1.re < 2⁻¹
  · simp [hupper]
  · simp [hupper]

of block trace powers. -/
theorem gradedBlockDiagonal_trace_pow
    (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (O : Matrix κ κ ℂ) (m : ℕ) :
    ((gradedBlockDiagonal C O) ^ m).trace =
      (C ^ m).trace + (O ^ m).trace := by
  rw [gradedBlockDiagonal_pow]
  simp [gradedBlockDiagonal, Matrix.trace, Fintype.sum_sum_type]

/-- Ordinary determinant of a graded block diagonal is the product of block determinants. -/
theorem gradedBlockDiagonal_det_one_sub
    (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (O : Matrix κ κ ℂ) (z : ℂ) :
    ((1 : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ) -
        z • gradedBlockDiagonal C O).det =
      ((1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) - z • C).det *
        ((1 : Matrix κ κ ℂ) - z • O).det := by
  have hblock : (1 : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ) -
      z • gradedBlockDiagonal C O =
      Matrix.fromBlocks ((1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) - z • C) 0 0
        ((1 : Matrix κ κ ℂ) - z • O) := by
    ext i j
    rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j <;>
      simp [gradedBlockDiagonal, Matrix.one_apply]
  rw [hblock]
  exact Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₁₂ _ _ _

/-- **Finite-window signed-trace rigidity.** Signed traces only through the total even rank
already force the complete determinant factorization. -/
theorem graded_signedTrace_preservation_le_forces_det_factor
    (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (O : Matrix κ κ ℂ)
    (E : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ)
    (htrace : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ Fintype.card (ι ⊕ κ) →
      (E ^ m).trace - (O ^ m).trace = (C ^ m).trace)
    (z : ℂ) :
    ((1 : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ) - z • E).det =
      ((1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) - z • C).det *
        ((1 : Matrix κ κ ℂ) - z • O).det := by
  have htrace' : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ Fintype.card (ι ⊕ κ) → (E ^ m).trace =
      ((gradedBlockDiagonal C O) ^ m).trace := by
    intro m hm
    rw [gradedBlockDiagonal_trace_pow]
    exact sub_eq_iff_eq_add.mp (htrace m hm)
  rw [det_one_sub_smul_eq_of_trace_pow_eq_le E (gradedBlockDiagonal C O) htrace' z]
  exact gradedBlockDiagonal_det_one_sub C O z

/-- **Signed-trace determinant rigidity.** Exact supertraces force exact determinant
factorization.  This is the cross-multiplied finite superdeterminant identity. -/
theorem graded_signedTrace_preservation_forces_det_factor
    (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (O : Matrix κ κ ℂ)
    (E : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ)
    (htrace : ∀ m : ℕ, (E ^ m).trace - (O ^ m).trace = (C ^ m).trace)
    (z : ℂ) :
    ((1 : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ) - z • E).det =
      ((1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) - z • C).det *
        ((1 : Matrix κ κ ℂ) - z • O).det := by
  have htrace' : ∀ m : ℕ, (E ^ m).trace =
      ((gradedBlockDiagonal C O) ^ m).trace := by
    intro m
    rw [gradedBlockDiagonal_trace_pow]
    exact sub_eq_iff_eq_add.mp (htrace m)
  rw [det_one_sub_smul_eq_of_trace_pow_eq E (gradedBlockDiagonal C O) htrace' z]
  exact gradedBlockDiagonal_det_one_sub C O z

/-- A real even divisor already locks the source divisor when signed traces are preserved only
through the total even rank. -/
theorem source_realDivisor_of_graded_signedTrace_le_realDivisor
    (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (O : Matrix κ κ ℂ)
    (E : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ)
    (htrace : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ Fintype.card (ι ⊕ κ) →
      (E ^ m).trace - (O ^ m).trace = (C ^ m).trace)
    (hreal : ∀ z : ℂ,
      ((1 : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ) - z • E).det = 0 → z.im = 0)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : ((1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) - z • C).det = 0) :
    z.im = 0 := by
  apply hreal z
  rw [graded_signedTrace_preservation_le_forces_det_factor C O E htrace z, hz, zero_mul]

/-- A real even divisor in an exact signed-trace lift forces the source divisor itself to be real. -/
theorem source_realDivisor_of_graded_signedTrace_realDivisor
    (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (O : Matrix κ κ ℂ)
    (E : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ)
    (htrace : ∀ m : ℕ, (E ^ m).trace - (O ^ m).trace = (C ^ m).trace)
    (hreal : ∀ z : ℂ,
      ((1 : Matrix (ι ⊕ κ) (ι ⊕ κ) ℂ) - z • E).det = 0 → z.im = 0)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : ((1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) - z • C).det = 0) :
    z.im = 0 := by
  apply hreal z
  rw [graded_signedTrace_preservation_forces_det_factor C O E htrace z, hz, zero_mul]

end

/-!
# First-order Lindblad channel additivity

This module formalizes the channel-additivity mechanism used in arXiv:2608.29858.
It applies to arbitrary finite jump families and arbitrary finite protocol schedules;
no positivity, perturbative approximation, or numerical calibration is assumed.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- Rate-weighted sum of a finite family of Lindblad generators. -/
def finiteLindbladFamilyDissipator
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (rate : ι → ℝ) (jump : ι → QuantumMatrix d) (X : QuantumMatrix d) :
    QuantumMatrix d :=
  ∑ i, (rate i : ℂ) • finiteLindbladDissipator (jump i) X

/-- Observable response of the complete channel family. -/
def finiteLindbladFamilyObservableResponse
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (rate : ι → ℝ) (jump : ι → QuantumMatrix d) (A X : QuantumMatrix d) : ℝ :=
  (Matrix.trace (A * finiteLindbladFamilyDissipator rate jump X)).re

/-- Damage convention for the complete channel family. -/
def finiteLindbladFamilyObservableDamage
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (rate : ι → ℝ) (jump : ι → QuantumMatrix d) (A X : QuantumMatrix d) : ℝ :=
  -finiteLindbladFamilyObservableResponse rate jump A X

/-- A weighted finite family remains trace preserving. -/
theorem trace_finiteLindbladFamilyDissipator
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (rate : ι → ℝ) (jump : ι → QuantumMatrix d) (X : QuantumMatrix d) :
    Matrix.trace (finiteLindbladFamilyDissipator rate jump X) = 0 := by
  simp [finiteLindbladFamilyDissipator, Matrix.trace_sum, Matrix.trace_smul,
    trace_finiteLindbladDissipator]

/-- First-order observable response is exactly additive across independent channels. -/
theorem finiteLindbladFamilyObservableResponse_eq_sum
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (rate : ι → ℝ) (jump : ι → QuantumMatrix d) (A X : QuantumMatrix d) :
    finiteLindbladFamilyObservableResponse rate jump A X =
      ∑ i, rate i * finiteLindbladObservableResponse (jump i) A X := by
  simp only [finiteLindbladFamilyObservableResponse, finiteLindbladFamilyDissipator,
    finiteLindbladObservableResponse, Matrix.mul_sum, Matrix.mul_smul,
    Matrix.trace_sum, Matrix.trace_smul]
  rw [Complex.re_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i hi
  simp [Complex.mul_re]

/-- The paper's damage convention inherits the same channel additivity. -/
theorem finiteLindbladFamilyObservableDamage_eq_sum
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (rate : ι → ℝ) (jump : ι → QuantumMatrix d) (A X : QuantumMatrix d) :
    finiteLindbladFamilyObservableDamage rate jump A X =
      ∑ i, rate i * finiteLindbladObservableDamage (jump i) A X := by
  rw [finiteLindbladFamilyObservableDamage,
    finiteLindbladFamilyObservableResponse_eq_sum]
  simp only [finiteLindbladObservableDamage]
  rw [← Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i hi
  ring

/-- Finite sampling model for an integrated first-order protocol cost. -/
structure RydbergFiniteFirstOrderProtocol
    (τ ι : Type*) [Fintype τ] [Fintype ι] (d : ℕ) where
  exposure : τ → ℝ
  rate : ι → ℝ
  jump : ι → QuantumMatrix d
  observable : τ → QuantumMatrix d
  state : τ → QuantumMatrix d

namespace RydbergFiniteFirstOrderProtocol

/-- Cost attributable to one channel over the complete protocol schedule. -/
def channelDamage
    {τ ι : Type*} [Fintype τ] [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (P : RydbergFiniteFirstOrderProtocol τ ι d) (i : ι) : ℝ :=
  ∑ t, P.exposure t *
    finiteLindbladObservableDamage (P.jump i) (P.observable t) (P.state t)

/-- Total cost obtained from the rate-weighted family generator at every schedule point. -/
def totalDamage
    {τ ι : Type*} [Fintype τ] [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (P : RydbergFiniteFirstOrderProtocol τ ι d) : ℝ :=
  ∑ t, P.exposure t *
    finiteLindbladFamilyObservableDamage P.rate P.jump (P.observable t) (P.state t)

/-- Exact protocol-level decomposition into channel-specific first-order costs. -/
theorem totalDamage_eq_sum_channelDamage
    {τ ι : Type*} [Fintype τ] [Fintype ι] {d : ℕ}
    (P : RydbergFiniteFirstOrderProtocol τ ι d) :
    P.totalDamage = ∑ i, P.rate i * P.channelDamage i := by
  rw [totalDamage]
  simp_rw [finiteLindbladFamilyObservableDamage_eq_sum]
  calc
    (∑ t, P.exposure t *
        ∑ i, P.rate i *
          finiteLindbladObservableDamage (P.jump i) (P.observable t) (P.state t)) =
        ∑ t, ∑ i, P.exposure t *
          (P.rate i *
            finiteLindbladObservableDamage (P.jump i) (P.observable t) (P.state t)) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro t ht
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    _ = ∑ i, ∑ t, P.exposure t *
          (P.rate i *
            finiteLindbladObservableDamage (P.jump i) (P.observable t) (P.state t)) :=
      Finset.sum_comm
    _ = ∑ i, P.rate i * P.channelDamage i := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i hi
      rw [channelDamage, Finset.mul_sum]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro t ht
      ring

/-!
# Exact Cauchy norm laws for every existing matrix jump generator

The genuine regularized jump, time derivative, space derivative, mixed
operator, and internally compatible second-time derivative are matrices
of ordinary L-infinity symbols. Their full norms and mutual distances are
preserved by the signed boundary Cauchy projection.
-/

open MeasureTheory Matrix
open scoped ENNReal

/-- The actual directJumpPerturbation written as a matrix of its own L-infinity symbols. -/
def directLinftyJumpMatrix (q : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x : ℝ) :
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) (Lp ℂ ∞ (volume : Measure ℝ)) :=
  regularizedLinftyJumpMatrix (directLinftySymbol q t x false) (directLinftySymbol q t x true)

/-- This matrix representation is exactly the previously implemented jump operator. -/
theorem directJumpPerturbation_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix (q : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x : ℝ) :
    directJumpPerturbation q t x = boundaryLinftyMatrix (directLinftyJumpMatrix q t x) := by
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro u
  change (-directMultiplier q t x false u.2,
    directMultiplier q t x true u.1 - directMultiplier q t x false (directMultiplier q t x true u.2)) =
      boundaryLinftyMatrix (regularizedLinftyJumpMatrix
        (directLinftySymbol q t x false) (directLinftySymbol q t x true)) u
  rw [boundaryLinftyMatrix_regularizedJump_apply]
  simp only [directMultiplier_eq_lineLinftyMultiplier]

/-- Cauchy compression preserves the complete norm of the actual directJumpPerturbation. -/
theorem norm_directCauchyOperator_eq_jump (q : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x : ℝ) :
    ‖directCauchyOperator q t x‖ = ‖directJumpPerturbation q t x‖ := by
  change ‖boundaryCauchy.comp (directJumpPerturbation q t x)‖ = _
  rw [directJumpPerturbation_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix, norm_boundaryCauchy_comp_boundaryLinftyMatrix]

/-- Approximation errors between any two members of this actual family retain their full norm. -/
theorem dist_directCauchyOperator_eq_jump (q p : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x s y : ℝ) :
    dist (directCauchyOperator q t x) (directCauchyOperator p s y) =
      dist (directJumpPerturbation q t x) (directJumpPerturbation p s y) := by
  change dist (boundaryCauchy.comp (directJumpPerturbation q t x))
    (boundaryCauchy.comp (directJumpPerturbation p s y)) = _
  rw [directJumpPerturbation_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix, directJumpPerturbation_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix]
  exact dist_boundaryCauchy_comp_boundaryLinftyMatrix _ _

/-- The actual directJumpTimeOperator written as a matrix of its own L-infinity symbols. -/
def directLinftyTimeMatrix (q : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x : ℝ) :
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) (Lp ℂ ∞ (volume : Measure ℝ)) :=
  offDiagonalLinftyMatrix (directTimeLinftySymbol q t x false) (directTimeLinftySymbol q t x true)

/-- This matrix representation is exactly the previously implemented jump operator. -/
theorem directJumpTimeOperator_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix (q : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x : ℝ) :
    directJumpTimeOperator q t x = boundaryLinftyMatrix (directLinftyTimeMatrix q t x) := by
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro u
  change (-directTimeMultiplier q t x false u.2, directTimeMultiplier q t x true u.1) =
    boundaryLinftyMatrix (offDiagonalLinftyMatrix
      (directTimeLinftySymbol q t x false) (directTimeLinftySymbol q t x true)) u
  rw [boundaryLinftyMatrix_offDiagonal_apply]
  simp only [directTimeMultiplier_eq_lineLinftyMultiplier]

/-- Cauchy compression preserves the complete norm of the actual directJumpTimeOperator. -/
theorem norm_directCauchyTimeOperator_eq_jump (q : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x : ℝ) :
    ‖directCauchyTimeOperator q t x‖ = ‖directJumpTimeOperator q t x‖ := by
  change ‖boundaryCauchy.comp (directJumpTimeOperator q t x)‖ = _
  rw [directJumpTimeOperator_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix, norm_boundaryCauchy_comp_boundaryLinftyMatrix]

/-- Approximation errors between any two members of this actual family retain their full norm. -/
theorem dist_directCauchyTimeOperator_eq_jump (q p : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x s y : ℝ) :
    dist (directCauchyTimeOperator q t x) (directCauchyTimeOperator p s y) =
      dist (directJumpTimeOperator q t x) (directJumpTimeOperator p s y) := by
  change dist (boundaryCauchy.comp (directJumpTimeOperator q t x))
    (boundaryCauchy.comp (directJumpTimeOperator p s y)) = _
  rw [directJumpTimeOperator_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix, directJumpTimeOperator_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix]
  exact dist_boundaryCauchy_comp_boundaryLinftyMatrix _ _

/-- Exact two-channel norm of the actual derivative, with no budget overestimate. -/
theorem norm_directJumpTimeOperator_eq_linfty (q : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (t x : ℝ) :
    ‖directJumpTimeOperator q t x‖ = max ‖directTimeLinftySymbol q t x false‖ ‖directTimeLinftySymbol q t x true‖ := by
  rw [directJumpTimeOperator_eq_boundaryLinftyMatrix]

    ((beta : ℂ) + (gam : ℂ) * I).re < 1 ∧
    c + 1 / 2 < 1

source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  intro s htotal
  let ray : Measure ℝ :=
    ENNReal.ofReal (thetaCuspLikelihoodRayWeight 2) •
      volume.restrict (Ioi (thetaCuspLikelihoodGap 2))
  have hrayLeAtom : ray ≤ thetaCuspAtomLikelihoodSpectralMeasure 2 := by
    unfold ray thetaCuspAtomLikelihoodSpectralMeasure
    exact Measure.le_add_left (le_refl _)
  have hatomLeTotal :
      thetaCuspAtomLikelihoodSpectralMeasure 2 ≤
        thetaCuspHigherLikelihoodSpectralMeasure := by
    unfold thetaCuspHigherLikelihoodSpectralMeasure
    simpa using
      (Measure.le_sum
        (fun k : ℕ => thetaCuspAtomLikelihoodSpectralMeasure (k + 2)) 0)
  have hrayZero : ray s = 0 := by
    apply bot_unique
    have hle := (hrayLeAtom.trans hatomLeTotal) s
    rw [htotal] at hle
    exact hle
  unfold ray at hrayZero
  rw [Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul,
    show thetaCuspLikelihoodGap 2 = 3 by norm_num [thetaCuspLikelihoodGap]] at hrayZero
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hrayZero).resolve_left
    (ne_of_gt (ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr
      (thetaCuspLikelihoodRayWeight_pos (n := 2) (by norm_num))))

theorem exists_bound_lintegral_sq_forcedProfile_block
    (hEdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ E (imStrip (-1) 1))
    (hE : ∀ z ∈ imStrip (-1) 1, E z ^ 2 = gammaRatio z)
    (hEne : ∀ z ∈ imStrip (-1) 1, E z ≠ 0) (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T)
    {σ : ℝ} (hσ0 : 0 < σ) (hσ1 : σ < 1) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (Y : ℝ), 1 < Y → ∀ (g : ℝ → X) (c : X) (m : ℝ),
      MemLp g 2 (volume : Measure ℝ) → StronglyMeasurable g →
      (∀ L : ℝ, L ∉ Icc m (m + 1) → g L = 0) →
      (∀ t : ℝ, Y ≤ |t| → ∀ L ∈ Icc m (m + 1), 1 ≤ wallFloor T σ t + L) →
      (∫⁻ x : ℝ, ‖forcedProfile E T (blockSource g m) c σ x‖ₑ ^ 2)
        ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * (‖c‖ ^ 2 + Y ^ 2 * ∫ L : ℝ, ‖g L‖ ^ 2))

theorem exists_bound_lintegral_sq_forcedProfile_block
    (hEdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ E (imStrip (-1) 1))
    (hE : ∀ z ∈ imStrip (-1) 1, E z ^ 2 = gammaRatio z)
    (hEne : ∀ z ∈ imStrip (-1) 1, E z ≠ 0) (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T)
    {σ : ℝ} (hσ0 : 0 < σ) (hσ1 : σ < 1) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (Y : ℝ), 1 < Y → ∀ (g : ℝ → X) (c : X) (m : ℝ),
      MemLp g 2 (volume : Measure ℝ) → StronglyMeasurable g →
      (∀ L : ℝ, L ∉ Icc m (m + 1) → g L = 0) →
      (∀ t : ℝ, Y ≤ |t| → ∀ L ∈ Icc m (m + 1), 1 ≤ wallFloor T σ t + L) →
      (∫⁻ x : ℝ, ‖forcedProfile E T (blockSource g m) c σ x‖ₑ ^ 2)
        ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * (‖c‖ ^ 2 + Y ^ 2 * ∫ L : ℝ, ‖g L‖ ^ 2))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨Cw, hCw, hwin⟩ :=
    exists_bound_lintegral_sq_forcedProfile_window hEdiff hE hEne hT hσ0 hσ1
  obtain ⟨Cn, hCn, hneg⟩ :=
    exists_bound_lintegral_sq_forcedProfile_negRay hEdiff hE hEne hT hσ0 hσ1
  obtain ⟨Cp, hCp, hpos⟩ :=
    exists_bound_lintegral_sq_forcedProfile_ray hEdiff hE hEne hT hσ0 hσ1
  refine ⟨Cw + Cn + Cp, by positivity, ?_⟩
  intro Y hY1 g c m hg2 hgm hsupp hfloor
  set N : ℝ := ∫ L : ℝ, ‖g L‖ ^ 2 with hNdef
  have hN0 : 0 ≤ N := integral_nonneg fun _ => by positivity
  have hS0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖c‖ ^ 2 + Y ^ 2 * N := by positivity

private theorem connesVanSuijlekomB2_target_not_extreme_of_det_pos
    (Q : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ) (hQ : Q.PosSemidef)
    (hH : connesVanSuijlekomB2HalfSpace Q) (hdet : 0 < Q.det) :
    ¬ IsExtremeRay connesVanSuijlekomB2TargetCone Q
source_arguments.source_statement:

    (Q : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ) (hQ : Q.PosSemidef)
    (hH : connesVanSuijlekomB2HalfSpace Q) (hdet : 0 < Q.det) :
    ¬ IsExtremeRay connesVanSuijlekomB2TargetCone Q
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  intro hExtreme
  have h10 : Q 1 0 = Q 0 1 := connesVanSuijlekomB2_offDiag_eq Q hQ
  have h11nonneg : 0 ≤ Q 1 1 := hQ.diag_nonneg
  have h11pos : 0 < Q 1 1 := by
    by_contra hnot
    have h11 : Q 1 1 = 0 := le_antisymm (le_of_not_gt hnot) h11nonneg
    have hsq : 0 ≤ Q 0 1 * Q 0 1 := mul_self_nonneg _
    rw [Matrix.det_fin_two, h10, h11] at hdet
    nlinarith
  let ε : ℝ := Q.det / (2 * Q 1 1)
  have hεpos : 0 < ε := by
    dsimp [ε]
    exact div_pos hdet (by positivity)
  have hBpsd : (ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00).PosSemidef :=
    connesVanSuijlekomB2_e00_posSemidef.smul hεpos.le
  have hCpsd : (Q - ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00).PosSemidef := by
    simpa [ε] using connesVanSuijlekomB2_sub_det_half_e00_posSemidef Q hQ hdet
  have hBH : connesVanSuijlekomB2HalfSpace (ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00) := by
    simp [connesVanSuijlekomB2HalfSpace, connesVanSuijlekomB2E00]
  have hCH : connesVanSuijlekomB2HalfSpace (Q - ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00) := by
    simpa [connesVanSuijlekomB2HalfSpace, connesVanSuijlekomB2E00] using hH
  have hB : ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00 ∈ connesVanSuijlekomB2TargetCone :=
    ⟨hBpsd, hBH⟩
  have hC : Q - ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00 ∈ connesVanSuijlekomB2TargetCone :=
    ⟨hCpsd, hCH⟩
  have hsum : ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00 + (Q - ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00) = Q := by
    abel
  obtain ⟨r, s, hr, hs, hBscale, hCscale⟩ :=
    hExtreme.2.2 _ _ hB hC hsum
  have hrzero : r = 0 := by
    have hentry := congrFun (congrFun hBscale 1) 1
    simp [connesVanSuijlekomB2E00] at hentry
    rcases hentry with hrzero | hQzero
    · exact hrzero
    · linarith
  have hBzero : ε • connesVanSuijlekomB2E00 = 0 := by
    simpa [hrzero] using hBscale
  have hentry := congrFun (congrFun hBzero 0) 0
  simp [connesVanSuijlekomB2E00] at hentry
  exact hεpos.ne' hentry

# Prime--archimedean universal strict-Hankel-ray adjoining law

## Status

In progress — paper proof and parent source exact-check complete; full Lean source check deferred
until final dependency build; literature novelty audit pending.

## Theorem-first provenance

- `RHTower/PrimeArchBlackHoleReciprocalSpectralConeUniversalityLaw.lean`
  - `primeArchBlackHoleReciprocalMixedClock_hankel_posDef_of_riemannHypothesis`
  - `riemannHypothesis_iff_primeArchBlackHoleReciprocal_spectralCone_posDef`
- `HTGeometry/DiscreteMomentHankel.lean`
  - `discreteMomentHankel_posDef`
- `HTGeometry/GeometricKallenLehmannResponse.lean`
  - `geometricKallenLehmannMoment_eq_tsum`
  - `geometricKallenLehmann_infiniteSupport`

## Universal law

Any moment ray whose Hankel matrix is positive definite at every finite depth can be adjoined to
the black-hole/reciprocal-continuum/prime--archimedean cone without changing its exact RH
classifier.  RH is equivalent to positive definiteness of every nonzero nonnegative four-ray
mixture.  The theorem quantifies over the adjoined strict ray, so it subsumes repeated one-off cone
extensions.

As a concrete cross-folder specialization, the self-similar geometric Källén--Lehmann response is
such a ray for every `0<a,b<1`.

## Paper proof

Hankel formation is linear.  Under RH the original three-ray mixture is positive definite whenever
one of its coefficients is positive.  Adding a nonnegative multiple of the fourth positive
semidefinite matrix preserves positive definiteness.  If the first three coefficients vanish, the
fourth coefficient is positive and its strictness supplies the result.  Conversely, set the fourth
coefficient to zero and recover the existing exact three-ray RH criterion.  The geometric
Källén--Lehmann specialization follows from its positive weights, summable moments, and nodes
escaping every finite set.

- **ID:** prime-arch-black-hole-reciprocal-spectral-cone-universality

- **Statement:** RH holds exactly when every nonzero nonnegative mixture of the normalized black-hole far-zone clock, reciprocal continuum clock, and normalized prime–archimedean moment clock has positive-definite Hankel matrices at every finite depth; under RH every such mixture escapes all fixed finite spectral and hidden-state dimensions.

## Goal

Adjoin the RH-sensitive prime--archimedean ray to the unconditional two-ray physical strict Hankel
cone and determine the exact resulting cone criterion.

## Approach

Under RH, the prime--archimedean Hankel matrix is positive definite in every degree by the Xi
central-moment criterion.  The black-hole and reciprocal matrices are unconditionally positive
definite.  A nonzero nonnegative combination of three positive-definite matrices is positive
definite: select a coefficient that is strictly positive and treat the remaining summands as
positive semidefinite.  Conversely, specialize the universal cone assertion to coefficients
`(0,0,1)`; determinant positivity on that pure prime--archimedean ray is exactly the existing RH
criterion.  Positive determinants also trigger the generic finite-spectral and finite-state-space
exclusion theorems.

# Unweighted Kummer-ray Hilbert augmentation

- **ID:** `deninger-unweighted-kummer-ray-hilbert-augmentation`
- **Stage:** 5-failed
- **Type:** FALSIFIED GREEN-DESCENT ROUTE
- **Label:** `DAC_UNWEIGHTED_KUMMER_RAY_HILBERT_AUGMENTATION_NO_GO`
- **Parent:** `deninger-kummer-poisson-green-boundary`
- **Claim tested:** suspend every projective Kummer harmonic ray,
  take their unweighted direct-sum Green energy, and descend to the
  single scalar radial Poisson complex by summing ray components.

## Hilbert quotient no-go

Let \(I\) be infinite, let \(H\ne0\) be a Hilbert space, and on the
finite-support direct sum define
\[
 \Sigma:\bigoplus_{i\in I}^{\mathrm{alg}}H\longrightarrow H,
 \qquad
 \Sigma((x_i))=\sum_i x_i.                                    \tag{1}
\]
Give the source the Hilbert direct-sum norm.

`[PROVED HERE]
[DAC_UNWEIGHTED_KUMMER_RAY_HILBERT_AUGMENTATION_NO_GO]`

The quotient seminorm induced by `(1)` is identically zero:
\[
 \inf_{\Sigma x=h}\sum_i\|x_i\|^2=0
 \qquad(h\in H).                                                \tag{2}
\]
Therefore the unweighted ray augmentation cannot transport a
strictly positive Green/Hodge metric to the scalar quotient.

### Proof

Choose \(N\) distinct indices and put \(x_i=h/N\) on them and zero
elsewhere.  Then \(\Sigma x=h\), while
\[
 \sum_i\|x_i\|^2
 =
 N\frac{\|h\|^2}{N^2}
 =
 \frac{\|h\|^2}{N}.
\]
Letting \(N\to\infty\) proves `(2)`.

## Weighted classification

For weights \(w=(w_i)\), define on finite-support vectors
\[
 \Sigma_w(x)=\sum_i\overline{w_i}x_i.                          \tag{3}
\]
This extends boundedly to \(\ell^2(I;H)\) exactly when
\(w\in\ell^2(I)\).  If \(w\ne0\), then
\[
 \inf_{\Sigma_wx=h}\|x\|_{\ell^2(I;H)}^2
 =
 \frac{\|h\|^2}{\|w\|_{\ell^2(I)}^2}.                          \tag{4}
\]

Indeed Cauchy--Schwarz gives the lower bound, and equality is attained
by
\[
 x_i=\frac{w_i}{\|w\|_2^2}h.
\]
Thus a nondegenerate Hilbert descent is equivalent to a nonzero
square-summable ray weight.

## Arithmetic consequence

Smooth suspension identifies each positive-rational orbit in the
nonzero Kummer lattice with one radial copy.  The algebraic
all-ones augmentation is canonical on finite-support nuclear
sections, but `(2)` proves that its Hilbert quotient loses all
positivity.

The missing source datum can therefore be stated sharply:
\[
 \boxed{\text{construct a canonical, Galois/correspondence-natural
 square-summable Kummer-ray density, or avoid raywise Hilbert
 quotienting.}}                                                \tag{5}
\]

No arbitrary enumeration or declared decaying weights are admissible.
The density must arise from the source Green operator, a transverse
measure/current, or a relative homological contraction before
completion.

## Strongest positive survivor

The unweighted sum remains continuous and meaningful on the
locally convex finite-support/nuclear direct sum.  Hence the valid
order remains:

1. smooth suspension and unit augmentation in the nuclear category;
2. take the scalar Poisson cohomology \(M_\zeta\);
3. descend a source-derived Green form only after proving its radical
   equals the augmentation kernel;
4. then complete the positive quotient.

Equivalently, a source transverse current may replace the raywise
Hilbert sum.  Its conservativity is part of the Hodge gate.

- It classifies exactly when a raywise Hilbert quotient is positive.
- It does not choose a weight or assume its existence.
- No zeta zero, RH premise, CCM object, or numerical computation is

# Kummer-ray smooth suspension resolution

- **ID:** `deninger-kummer-ray-smooth-suspension-resolution`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** SOURCE NUCLEAR-SUSPENSION THEOREM
- **Labels:** `DAC_KUMMER_RAY_SMOOTH_SUSPENSION`,
  `DAC_KUMMER_RAY_AUGMENTATION_RESOLUTION`
- **Parent:** `deninger-poisson-hodge-polarization`
- **Statement:** smooth suspension converts every positive-rational
  Kummer orbit into an ordinary radial copy with strongly continuous
  flow; canonical nuclear augmentation has a strict two-term
  resolution whose quotient is exactly one scalar radial sector.

## 1. Orbitwise radialization

Let
\[
 V=
 (\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\times}/\mu_\infty)
 \otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q
\]
and let \(f_a\in H_{\mathrm{Kum}}\) be the logarithmic Kummer vector.
For \(a\ne0\), put
\[
 r(a)=\|f_a\|>0.
\]
Positive rational powers satisfy
\[
 r(qa)=q\,r(a).                                                 \tag{1}
\]
Let
\[
 \mathbb P_+(V)
 =
 (V\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb Q_{>0}.
\]
On \((V\setminus\{0\})\times\mathbb R_{>0}\), use Deninger's deck
relation
\[
 (a,u)\sim(qa,u/q).                                             \tag{2}
\]

`[PROVED HERE] [DAC_KUMMER_RAY_SMOOTH_SUSPENSION]`

The map
\[
 [(a,u)]
 \longmapsto
 \left([a],x=u\,r(a)\right)                                    \tag{3}
\]
is a bijection
\[
 \left((V\setminus\{0\})\times\mathbb R_{>0}\right)/
 \mathbb Q_{>0}
 \cong
 \mathbb P_+(V)\times\mathbb R_{>0}.                            \tag{4}
\]
Under `(4)`, Deninger's flow is
\[
 \phi^t([a],x)=([a],e^tx).                                     \tag{5}
\]

### Proof

Equation `(1)` makes \(x\) invariant under `(2)`:
\[
 (u/q)r(qa)=ur(a).
\]
Thus `(3)` is well defined.  If two pairs have the same ray and
same \(x\), write \(b=qa\).  Equality of \(ur(a)\) and \(vr(b)\)
gives \(v=u/q\), so they are equivalent.  Surjectivity follows by
choosing any representative of a ray and taking \(u=x/r(a)\).
Formula `(5)` is immediate.

## 2. Nuclear smooth sections

Let \(H_-\) be Meyer's all-weight radial Schwartz space.  Define the
locally convex direct sum
\[
 \mathscr S_{\mathrm{ray}}
 =
 \bigoplus_{[a]\in\mathbb P_+(V)} H_- .                         \tag{6}
\]
Elements have finite ray support and a nuclear radial component.
The flow acts componentwise by Meyer's dilation.

Because each element has finite ray support and dilation is strongly
continuous on \(H_-\), `(5)` defines a strongly continuous
representation on `(6)`.  This is the smooth/nuclear survivor of
`DAC_BARE_KUMMER_MODE_ELL2_FLOW_NO_GO`: the suspension-height
variable is retained before completion.

Galois maps permute the ray index.  Positive-rational power maps act
trivially on the ray after deck descent and act through radial
dilation before descent.  Hence the construction is
Galois-, power-, and flow-natural.

## 3. Canonical unit augmentation

Define
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{ray}}:
 \mathscr S_{\mathrm{ray}}\longrightarrow H_-,
 \qquad
 (h_{[a]})\longmapsto\sum_{[a]}h_{[a]}.                        \tag{7}
\]
The sum is finite.

`[PROVED HERE] [DAC_KUMMER_RAY_AUGMENTATION_RESOLUTION]`

The sequence
\[
 0\longrightarrow
 K_{\mathrm{ray}}
 \longrightarrow
 \mathscr S_{\mathrm{ray}}
 \xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ray}}}
 H_-
 \longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 K_{\mathrm{ray}}=\ker\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ray}},              \tag{8}
\]
is strict exact in complete locally convex spaces after taking the
standard completed locally convex direct sum.  It is equivariant for
flow and Galois action.

Equivalently, the two-term complex
\[
 K_{\mathrm{ray}}
 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{incl}}
 \mathscr S_{\mathrm{ray}}                                     \tag{9}
\]
has only degree-zero cohomology, canonically \(H_-\).

### Proof

Continuity of `(7)` is the universal property of the locally convex
direct sum.  It is surjective: for any chosen ray \(r_0\), placing
\(h\) in the \(r_0\)-summand gives a continuous linear section.
Existence of a continuous section proves openness and strictness;
the quotient and its identification with \(H_-\) are independent of
the chosen section.  Equivariance follows because Galois maps only
permute a finite support and dilation commutes with finite summation.
The cohomology statement is exactly strict exactness of `(8)`.

The same construction with \(H_\cap\) in degree zero commutes with
Meyer's operator:
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{ray}}\!
 \left((Zh_{[a]})_{[a]}\right)
 =
 Z\!\left(\sum_{[a]}h_{[a]}\right).                            \tag{10}
\]
Thus the augmentation resolution can be attached before the
Poisson differential and produces one, not ray-many, copies of the
Poisson complex.

## 4. Exact Green frontier

The local Green energies from
`DAC_KUMMER_PHASE_POISSON_GREEN_BOUNDARY` define positive diagonal
forms before augmentation.  They do not descend by the naive Hilbert
quotient: `DAC_UNWEIGHTED_KUMMER_RAY_HILBERT_AUGMENTATION_NO_GO`
proves that the induced quotient seminorm would be zero.

# Suzuki--Mangoldt apex ray isolation

- **ID:** `suzuki-mangoldt-apex-ray-isolation`
- **Stage:** 3 — formalized in Lean 4
- **Type:** frontier falsifier / exact source classification / positive survivor
- **Parent:** `suzuki-positive-arch-mangoldt-quadrature-deficit.md`

## Question

At width `L = log 2`, aperture `a_n = log(2n)/2`, the Mangoldt node
`tau_n = 2 log n` is the unique positive-lag apex of the Suzuki sample channel.  Can its missing
pointwise transport mass be paid by flank atoms in the same Euler valuation ray?

## Exact proposed classification

For integers `n,m >= 2`, prove

```text
A_(a_n)(tau_m)
 =sqrt(m) max(0, log 2-|log(m/n)|).                       (AR1)
```

Consequently the aligned channel is supported exactly on the multiplicative annulus
`n/2 < m < 2n`.  For one prime-power ray `m=2^j`, `n=2^k`, the only exponent in this open annulus
is `j=k`; the neighboring valuations `2^(k-1)` and `2^(k+1)` lie at the zero boundary.  Hence

```text
A_(a_(2^k))(tau_(2^j))>0  iff  j=k.                      (AR2)
```

## Frontier consequence

If `(AR2)` holds, primewise/valuation-diagonal apex blocks are impossible.  The apex atom is
isolated inside its own Euler ray, so every viable `SUZUKI-APEX-BLOCK-TRANSPORT` must mix distinct
prime labels before positivity or capacity-one transport is imposed.  This is stronger than the
existing pointwise-cell no-go, which allows an unspecified block source.

The positive survivor is the exact annular kernel `(AR1)`: it identifies the only legal flank
pool and turns the next problem into a cross-prime block incidence theorem on
`n/2 < m < 2n`, with the restricted-Weil/Robin boundary channel retained.

## Falsifiers

- Any same-ray exponent `j != k` with positive aligned channel value falsifies `(AR2)`.
- A proof which uses only unique maximality does not establish ray isolation; the zero support
  boundary at ratios `1/2` and `2` is load-bearing.
- Cross-prime mixing is a conclusion only after `(AR1)` is derived from the actual rectangular
  channel, not from a replacement tent.

## Proof

The positive channel is the sum of its fixed and moving tents.  At
`L=log 2`, `t=2 log m`, and `m>=2`, the fixed height is

```text
log 2 - t/2 = log 2 - log m <= 0,
```

so the fixed channel vanishes.  At aperture `a_n=log(2n)/2`, the moving center is

```text
2a_n-log 2 = log n.
```

Its exponential prefactor is `exp(t/4)=exp(log m/2)=sqrt m`; substituting these two
identities into the actual channel gives `(AR1)`.

The positive support condition is

```text
|log(m/n)| < log 2,
```

equivalently `n/2<m<2n`.  If `m=b^j`, `n=b^k`, `b>=2`, and `j!=k`, the larger power is
at least `b` times the smaller, hence at least twice the smaller.  It lies outside the open
annulus (on its boundary when `b=2` and the exponents are adjacent), so its sample is zero.
At `j=k`, `(AR1)` is `sqrt(b^k) log 2>0`.  This proves `(AR2)` for every base `b>=2`,
strictly stronger than the proposed dyadic statement.

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.LinearPMapUnitarySquareTransport
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.SuzukiCanonicalHankelCompressionBridge
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.WeightOneCliffordLogClosure

/-!
# Closed weight-one Clifford--Dirac operator on the positive ray

This module transports the closed log-line realization to Suzuki's literal
`L²((0,∞), dt)` carrier. The exact natural square domain and composition identity are transported
together with the operators; the square remains self-adjoint.
-/

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped ENNReal LinearPMap

namespace RHTower

/-- Closed weight-one Dirac realization on literal `L²((0,∞), dt)`. -/
def weightOnePositiveDirac (a : ℝ) : SuzukiPositiveL2 →ₗ.[ℂ] SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.unitaryConjugateLinearPMap suzukiPositiveLogUnitary
    (weightOneLogDirac a)

/-- Literal positive-ray square transported from the self-adjoint log-line square. -/
def weightOnePositiveSquare (a : ℝ) : SuzukiPositiveL2 →ₗ.[ℂ] SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.unitaryConjugateLinearPMap suzukiPositiveLogUnitary
    (weightOneLogSquare a)

/-- Integer-order Sobolev domain on the positive ray, transported by logarithmic half-density
coordinates from the standard Fourier domain on `L²(ℝ)`. -/
def weightOnePositiveSobolevDomain (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  (fourierL2SobolevDomain n).comap suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap

/-- Transported `H¹` domain on `L²((0,∞), dt)`. -/
abbrev weightOnePositiveH1 : Submodule ℂ SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  weightOnePositiveSobolevDomain 1

/-- Transported `H²` domain on `L²((0,∞), dt)`. -/
abbrev weightOnePositiveH2 : Submodule ℂ SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  weightOnePositiveSobolevDomain 2

/-- Closed centered scale generator on the positive ray, obtained from the weak log derivative. -/
def weightOnePositiveCenteredGenerator : SuzukiPositiveL2 →ₗ.[ℂ] SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.unitaryConjugateLinearPMap suzukiPositiveLogUnitary
    weightOneLogDerivative

/-- Weight-one inversion `J`, transported from reflection in logarithmic coordinates. -/
def weightOnePositiveInversion : SuzukiPositiveL2 →L[ℂ] SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.symm.toLinearIsometry.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L
    l2Reflection ∘L
      suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.toLinearIsometry.toContinuousLinearMap

@[simp] theorem weightOnePositiveInversion_apply (f : SuzukiPositiveL2) :
    weightOnePositiveInversion f =
      suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.symm (l2Reflection (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary f)) := rfl

/-- Positive-ray inversion is an involution. -/
@[simp] theorem weightOnePositiveInversion_involutive (f : SuzukiPositiveL2) :
    weightOnePositiveInversion (weightOnePositiveInversion f) = f := by
  apply suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.injective
  simp only [weightOnePositiveInversion_apply, LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply,
    l2Reflection_involutive]

/-- Positive-ray inversion preserves the `L²` norm. -/
theorem weightOnePositiveInversion_norm (f : SuzukiPositiveL2) :
    ‖weightOnePositiveInversion f‖ = ‖f‖ := by
  calc
    ‖weightOnePositiveInversion f‖ = ‖l2Reflection (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary f)‖ := by
      rw [weightOnePositiveInversion_apply, suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.symm.norm_map]
    _ = ‖suzukiPositiveLogUnitary f‖ := by
      change ‖l2ReflectionIsometry (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary f)‖ = _
      exact l2ReflectionIsometry.norm_map _
    _ = ‖f‖ := suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.norm_map f

/-- Positive-ray inversion is symmetric, hence bounded self-adjoint in the Hilbert-space sense. -/
theorem weightOnePositiveInversion_symmetric :
    weightOnePositiveInversion.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric := by
  intro f g
  calc
    inner ℂ (weightOnePositiveInversion f) g =
        inner ℂ (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary (weightOnePositiveInversion f))
          (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary g) :=
      (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.inner_map_map _ _).symm
    _ = inner ℂ (l2Reflection (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary f))
          (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary g) := by
      rw [weightOnePositiveInversion_apply, LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    _ = inner ℂ (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary f)
          (l2Reflection (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary g)) :=
      l2Reflection_symmetric _ _
    _ = inner ℂ (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary f)
          (suzukiPositiveLogUnitary (weightOnePositiveInversion g)) := by
      rw [weightOnePositiveInversion_apply, LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    _ = inner ℂ f (weightOnePositiveInversion g) :=
      suzukiPositiveLogUnitary.inner_map_map _ _

/-- Reciprocal transport of the positive-ray measure is quasi-measure-preserving. -/
theorem positiveReciprocal_quasiMeasurePreserving :
    Measure.QuasiMeasurePreserving (fun x : ℝ => x⁻¹)
      (volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ))) volume := by
  have hcomp := realExp_quasiMeasurePreserving.comp
    ((Measure.measurePreserving_neg (volume : Measure ℝ)).quasiMeasurePreserving.comp

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.DeningerPreimageZeroMass

/-!
# The even extension of the canonical Möbius preimage

The commutator of the card is built from the *even* extension `E f_h` of the ray preimage.  Taking
the absolute value of the argument is the extension, and evenness is then definitional.

Reflection of the line carries the negative ray onto the positive one, so the extension inherits
the ray estimates: its mass on each half is the ray mass, which is zero.

* `deningerEvenPreimage` : the even extension `E f_h`.
* `deningerEvenPreimage_even` : it is even.
* `deningerEvenPreimage_of_pos` : on the positive ray it is the preimage itself.
* `deningerEvenPreimage_integrableOn_Iio` : reflection transports integrability to the negative ray.
-/

namespace RHTower

open MeasureTheory SchwartzMap

noncomputable section

/-- **The even extension of the canonical Möbius preimage.** -/
def deningerEvenPreimage (h : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (x : ℝ) : ℂ := deningerMobiusPreimage h |x|

@[simp]
theorem deningerEvenPreimage_even (h : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (x : ℝ) :
    deningerEvenPreimage h (-x) = deningerEvenPreimage h x := by
  rw [deningerEvenPreimage, deningerEvenPreimage, abs_neg]

theorem deningerEvenPreimage_of_pos (h : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) :
    deningerEvenPreimage h x = deningerMobiusPreimage h x := by
  rw [deningerEvenPreimage, abs_of_pos hx]

theorem deningerEvenPreimage_of_neg (h : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) {x : ℝ} (hx : x < 0) :
    deningerEvenPreimage h x = deningerMobiusPreimage h (-x) := by
  rw [deningerEvenPreimage, abs_of_neg hx]

/-- Reflection carries the negative ray onto the positive one. -/
theorem deningerNeg_preimage_Ioi : (fun x : ℝ => -x) ⁻¹' Set.Ioi 0 = Set.Iio 0 := by
  ext x
  simp [Set.mem_Iio]

/-- **Reflection transports integrability from the positive ray to the negative one.** -/
theorem deningerEvenPreimage_integrableOn_Iio {g : ℝ → ℂ}
    (hg : IntegrableOn g (Set.Ioi 0)) :
    IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ => g (-x)) (Set.Iio 0) := by
  have hmp : MeasurePreserving (fun x : ℝ => -x) volume volume :=
    Measure.measurePreserving_neg volume
  have hme : MeasurableEmbedding (fun x : ℝ => -x) :=
    (Homeomorph.neg ℝ).measurableEmbedding
  have hiff := hmp.integrableOn_comp_preimage hme (f := g) (s := Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))
  rw [deningerNeg_preimage_Ioi] at hiff
  exact hiff.mpr hg

end

end RHTower

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.MultipleEllipticGammaPeriodRankDichotomy

/-!
# Period families on a rational ray exist

The rank dichotomy sorts period families by whether they lie on one rational ray through an
upper-half-plane direction.  That side of the dichotomy is inhabited: any rational multiple family
of a fixed upper-half-plane direction lies on its ray, and the constant family of the imaginary
unit is the simplest instance.  A rational ray is in particular a rational affine line, with zero
affine part, once the rational coefficients are positive.
-/

open Complex

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

variable {ι : Type}

/-- **Every rational multiple family lies on a rational ray.** -/
theorem multipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalRay_ratSmul (c : ι → ℚ) {ω : ℂ} (hω : 0 < ω.im) :
    MultipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalRay (fun i => (c i : ℂ) * ω) :=
  ⟨ω, hω, c, fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- The constant family of the imaginary unit lies on a rational ray. -/
theorem multipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalRay_const_I :
    MultipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalRay (fun _ : ι => Complex.I) := by
  refine ⟨Complex.I, by simp, fun _ => (1 : ℚ), fun i => ?_⟩
  simp

/-- The rational-ray condition is inhabited for every index type. -/
theorem exists_multipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalRay :
    ∃ τ : ι → ℂ, MultipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalRay τ :=
  ⟨fun _ => Complex.I, multipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalRay_const_I⟩

/-- A rational ray with positive coefficients is a rational affine line with zero affine part. -/
theorem multipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalAffineLine_of_ratSmul
    (c : ι → ℚ) (hc : ∀ i, 0 < c i) {ω : ℂ} (hω : 0 < ω.im) :
    MultipleEllipticGammaLiesOnRationalAffineLine (fun i => (c i : ℂ) * ω) := by
  refine ⟨ω, hω, fun _ => 0, c, hc, fun i => ?_⟩
  simp

end

end GaloisForLFunctions

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.WeightedEulerMobiusDecayTransfer
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.LambertRayRecovery
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.CompactCarrierLambert

/-!
# Quantitative Möbius recovery along a multiplicative ray

The decay companion of `fourierBorel_eq_zero_of_lambert_ray_zero`: if a
function decays geometrically along the multiplicative ray `{n·x}` and its
positive Lambert derivative is exponentially small there (`≤ D·ρⁿ`,
`ρ ≤ 1/2`), then Möbius inversion bounds the first ray value:

`‖F x‖ ≤ 4·D·ρ`.

Composed with `positiveLambertDerivative_compactFourierBorel`, this converts
sampled decay of the compact-carrier Lambert transform into decay of the
Fourier–Borel transform itself — the step from the oversampled sampling bound
to the carrier-separation hypothesis.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- **Quantitative Möbius ray recovery**: geometric ray decay of `F` plus
exponential smallness of its positive Lambert derivative bound the first ray
value with the explicit constant `4`. -/
theorem norm_fourierBorel_le_of_lambert_ray_decay
    (F : ℂ → ℂ) (x : ℂ) {C r D ρ : ℝ}
    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r < 1)
    (hdecay : ∀ n : ℕ+, ‖F ((n : ℂ) * x)‖ ≤ C * r ^ (n : ℕ))
    (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ) (hρhalf : ρ ≤ 1 / 2)
    (hH : ∀ n : ℕ+,
      ‖positiveLambertDerivative F ((n : ℂ) * x)‖ ≤ D * ρ ^ (n : ℕ)) :
    ‖F x‖ ≤ 4 * D * ρ := by
  have h := norm_first_le_of_weightedLambert_decay
    (fun n : ℕ+ => F ((n : ℂ) * x)) hC hr0 hr1 hdecay hD hρ0 hρhalf
    (fun n => by
      rw [weightedLambertTransform_ray_eq]
      exact hH n)
  simpa using h

/-- The compact-carrier form: sampled decay of the Lambert transform along
the ray `{n·x}` bounds the Fourier–Borel transform at `x`. -/
theorem norm_compactFourierBorel_le_of_sampled_lambert_decay
    {K : Type*} [TopologicalSpace K] [CompactSpace K]
    (L : C(K, ℂ) →L[ℂ] ℂ) (s : C(K, ℂ)) (x : ℂ)
    (hq : ∀ n : ℕ+, ‖compactExponentialTest s ((n : ℂ) * x)‖ < 1)
    {C r D ρ : ℝ}
    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r < 1)
    (hdecay : ∀ n : ℕ+,
      ‖compactFourierBorel L s ((n : ℂ) * x)‖ ≤ C * r ^ (n : ℕ))
    (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ) (hρhalf : ρ ≤ 1 / 2)
    (hlam : ∀ n : ℕ+,
      ‖compactCarrierLambertTransform L s ((n : ℂ) * x)‖ ≤ D * ρ ^ (n : ℕ)) :
    ‖compactFourierBorel L s x‖ ≤ 4 * D * ρ := by
  apply norm_fourierBorel_le_of_lambert_ray_decay
    (compactFourierBorel L s) x hC hr0 hr1 hdecay hD hρ0 hρhalf
  intro n
  rw [positiveLambertDerivative_compactFourierBorel L s _ (hq n)]
  exact hlam n

end RHTower

lemma sameRay_nonneg_smul_right (v : M) (h : 0 ≤ a) : SameRay R v (a • v) := by

/-- If two vectors are on the same ray then they remain so after applying a linear map. -/
theorem map (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (h : SameRay R x y) : SameRay R (f x) (f y) :=

/-- The images of two vectors under an injective linear map are on the same ray if and only if the
original vectors are on the same ray. -/
theorem _root_.Function.Injective.sameRay_map_iff
    {F : Type*} [FunLike F M N] [LinearMapClass F R M N]

original vectors are on the same ray. -/

  Function.Injective.sameRay_map_iff (EquivLike.injective e)

/-- If `x` and `y` are on the same ray as `z`, then so is `x + y`. -/

          (shiftedMomentHankelMatrix moment N) +
        density N N * moment (2 * N + 2) +
        ∑ i : Fin N, (density N i + density i N) *
          moment (N + i + 2) := by
  unfold matrixDensityPair finiteDensitySection shiftedMomentHankelMatrix

        ∑ i : Fin N, density N i * moment (N + i + 2) := by
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i hi
    congr 2
    omega
  rw [hcross]
  ring_nf

/-- A density reader is cyclic against a clock when the clock may be moved across every observed
matrix without changing the density pairing. -/
def MatrixDensityClockCyclic
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (density : Matrix I I ℝ) (clock : I → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Matrix I I ℝ,
    matrixDensityPair density (Matrix.diagonal clock * A) =
      matrixDensityPair density (A * Matrix.diagonal clock)

@[simp] theorem matrixDensityPair_single
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (density : Matrix I I ℝ) (i j : I) (x : ℝ) :
    matrixDensityPair density (Matrix.single i j x) = density j i * x := by
  unfold matrixDensityPair
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
  · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single j]
    · simp
    · intro b hb hbj
      simp [Ne.symm hbj]
    · simp
  · intro a ha hai
    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    intro b hb
    simp [Ne.symm hai]
  · simp

/-- Cyclicity against one simple-spectrum clock already forces the density to be diagonal in that
clock basis.  Full-matrix cyclicity is not required. -/
theorem matrixDensityClockCyclic_offDiagonal_eq_zero
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (density : Matrix I I ℝ) (clock : I → ℝ)
    (hclock : Function.Injective clock)
    (hcyc : MatrixDensityClockCyclic density clock)
    {i j : I} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    density i j = 0 := by
  have h := hcyc (Matrix.single j i 1)
  have hleft :
      Matrix.diagonal clock * Matrix.single j i 1 =
        Matrix.single j i (clock j) := by
    ext a b
    rw [Matrix.diagonal_mul]
    by_cases hja : j = a <;> by_cases hib : i = b <;>
      simp [hja, hib]
  have hright :
      Matrix.single j i 1 * Matrix.diagonal clock =
        Matrix.single j i (clock i) := by
    ext a b
    rw [Matrix.mul_diagonal]
    by_cases hja : j = a <;> by_cases hib : i = b <;>
      simp [hja, hib]
  rw [hleft, hright, matrixDensityPair_single, matrixDensityPair_single] at h
  have hne : clock j - clock i ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (hclock.ne hij.symm)
  have hzero : (clock j - clock i) * density i j = 0 := by
    linarith
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hzero).resolve_left hne

          2 * ∑ j : Fin n,
            hankelToeplitzCounterweight moment
                ((n + 1) - ((j : ℕ) + 1)) *
              moment ((n + 1) + ((j : ℕ) + 1) + 2)) /
        (2 * moment (n + 3))

    (moment : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hmoment : moment (n + 3) ≠ 0) :
    moment (2 * (n + 1) + 2) +

              ((n + 1) - (i : ℕ)) *
            moment ((n + 1) + (i : ℕ) + 2) = 0 := by
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]
  simp only [Fin.val_zero, Nat.sub_zero, add_zero, Fin.val_succ]
  rw [hankelToeplitzCounterweight_succ]
  field_simp

/-!
# The moment-bound crossing for zero-density estimates

For a Dirichlet polynomial of length `N` at height `T = N^{τ}` with `τ ∈ (k, k+1)`, two moment bounds
compete: raising to the `k+1`-st power (valid once `N^{k+1} ≥ T`) and the `k`-th mean value (valid
while `N^{k} ≤ T`).  They agree at `τ = k + 2 - 2σ`, and there the common value exceeds the
density-hypothesis target `(2 - 2σ)τ` by `(2 - 2σ)(2σ - 1)`, a quantity **independent of `k`**.
-/

/-- The "power" branch of the moment bound on the window `(k, k+1)`: raising to the `k+1`-st power. -/
noncomputable def powerBranch (σ k : ℝ) : ℝ := (k + 1) * (2 - 2 * σ)

/-- The "mean value" branch of the moment bound at abscissa `τ`. -/
noncomputable def meanValueBranch (σ k τ : ℝ) : ℝ := τ + k * (1 - 2 * σ)

/-- The Density-Hypothesis requirement at abscissa `τ`. -/
noncomputable def densityTarget (σ τ : ℝ) : ℝ := (2 - 2 * σ) * τ

/-- The two moment branches agree at `τ = k + 2 - 2σ`. -/
theorem powerBranch_eq_meanValueBranch (σ k : ℝ) :
    powerBranch σ k = meanValueBranch σ k (k + 2 - 2 * σ) := by
  unfold powerBranch meanValueBranch
  ring

/-- At the crossing `τ = k + 2 - 2σ` the moment bound exceeds the Density-Hypothesis target by
`(2 - 2σ)(2σ - 1)`, **independently of `k`**. -/
theorem crossing_shortfall (σ k : ℝ) :
    powerBranch σ k - densityTarget σ (k + 2 - 2 * σ) = (2 - 2 * σ) * (2 * σ - 1) := by
  unfold powerBranch densityTarget
  ring

/-- The shortfall is positive exactly when `1/2 < σ < 1`. -/
theorem crossing_shortfall_pos {σ : ℝ} (h₁ : 1 / 2 < σ) (h₂ : σ < 1) (k : ℝ) :
    0 < powerBranch σ k - densityTarget σ (k + 2 - 2 * σ) := by
  rw [crossing_shortfall]
  have h3 : 0 < 2 - 2 * σ := by linarith
  have h4 : 0 < 2 * σ - 1 := by linarith
  positivity

/-
The Plancherel density gap, and why the sixth moment inside Motohashi's identity is unreachable.

Motohashi's explicit formula for the error term in the fourth moment of `ζ` weights the spectrum by
`T^{1/2} r^{-3/2}`.  On the cuspidal spectrum the counting measure has density `≍ r dr`; on the
Eisenstein spectrum the Plancherel measure has density `≍ dr`.  The continuous term is therefore
suppressed by a full factor of `r` relative to the cuspidal one.

Consequences, all pure exponent arithmetic:

* the cuspidal sum has weight-plus-density exponent `-1/2 > -1`, so it is dominated by the **top** of
  the spectral range — which is why the cubic moment of cusp forms is what the identity sees;
* the continuous integral has exponent `-3/2 < -1`, so it converges and is dominated by the
  **bottom**, `r = O(1)`.  The sixth moment of `ζ` at large height never enters;
* even granting positivity of the spectral weight, the bound obtainable for the sixth moment at
  height `R` from the fourth moment at height `T = R²` is `R^{3/2}` at best — worse than the known
  `R^{5/4}`.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.MomentChordPivot

namespace HTGeometry

/-- Exponent of the spectral weight in Motohashi's explicit formula: `T^{1/2} r^{-3/2}`. -/
def motohashiWeightExponent : ℚ := -3/2

/-- Density exponent of the cuspidal spectrum of `GL(2)`: the Weyl law gives `≍ r dr`. -/
def cuspidalDensityExponent : ℚ := 1

/-- Density exponent of the Eisenstein spectrum of `GL(2)`: the Plancherel measure is `≍ dr`. -/
def eisensteinDensityExponent : ℚ := 0

/-- **The Plancherel density gap.**  The continuous spectrum carries one power of `r` less than the
cuspidal spectrum; this single exponent is the whole obstruction. -/
theorem plancherel_density_gap :
    cuspidalDensityExponent - eisensteinDensityExponent = 1 := by
  unfold cuspidalDensityExponent eisensteinDensityExponent; norm_num

/-- The cuspidal sum is top-dominated: its integrand exponent exceeds `-1`. -/
theorem cuspidal_top_dominated :
    -1 < motohashiWeightExponent + cuspidalDensityExponent := by
  unfold motohashiWeightExponent cuspidalDensityExponent; norm_num

/-- The continuous integral is bottom-dominated: its integrand exponent is below `-1`, so it
converges and is governed by `r = O(1)`.  The sixth moment at large height is invisible to it. -/
theorem eisenstein_bottom_dominated :
    motohashiWeightExponent + eisensteinDensityExponent < -1 := by
  unfold motohashiWeightExponent eisensteinDensityExponent; norm_num

/-- Output exponent of the positivity route: from `E₂(T) ≪ T^{e}` and the weight `T^{1/2}R^{-3/2}`,
with the spectral range capped at `R ≤ T^{1/2}` so that `T = R²`, the sixth moment at height `R` is
bounded by `R^{2e - 1 + 3/2}`. -/
def positivityRouteOutput (e : ℚ) : ℚ := 2 * e - 1 + 3/2

/-- With the known bound `E₂(T) ≪ T^{2/3}` the route gives `11/6`. -/
theorem positivityRouteOutput_known : positivityRouteOutput (2/3) = 11/6 := by
  unfold positivityRouteOutput; norm_num

/-- With the conjectured, `Ω`-matching bound `E₂(T) ≪ T^{1/2+ε}` — which cannot be improved, since
`E₂(T) = Ω_±(T^{1/2})` — the route gives `3/2`. -/
theorem positivityRouteOutput_optimal : positivityRouteOutput (1/2) = 3/2 := by
  unfold positivityRouteOutput; norm_num

/-- **The ceiling.**  Even at the `Ω`-imposed floor for `E₂`, the positivity route returns `3/2`,
strictly worse than the known moment envelope value `5/4 = momentChord 6`.  So the route is void:
it cannot be made to work, and would be worthless if it could. -/
theorem positivity_route_void :
    momentChord (2 * 3) < positivityRouteOutput (1/2) ∧
    momentChord (2 * 3) < positivityRouteOutput (2/3) := by
  constructor
  · rw [positivityRouteOutput_optimal]; unfold momentChord; norm_num
  · rw [positivityRouteOutput_known]; unfold momentChord; norm_num

/-- The route improves on the envelope only for `E₂(T) ≪ T^{e}` with `e < 3/8`, below the `Ω`-result
`E₂(T) = Ω_±(T^{1/2})`.  So the obstruction is an `Ω`-result, not a lack of effort. -/
theorem positivity_route_threshold {e : ℚ} :
    positivityRouteOutput e < 5/4 ↔ e < 3/8 := by
  unfold positivityRouteOutput
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

end HTGeometry

  have hinv : (↑r⁻¹ : A) * z = z * r⁻¹ := by

      _ = ((↑r⁻¹ : A) * r) * z * r⁻¹ := by noncomm_ring

  simp [reciprocalCommutatorHistory, h, hinv]

    {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)

    (hflat : xiShiftedMomentHankelMatrix y (n + 1) *ᵥ
      HTGeometry.monicMomentAdmissionVector
        (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) n = 0) :
    HasDerivAt (fun v => xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionOddCurrent v n)
      (-2 * xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveShear y n) y
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let s : ℕ → ℝ := fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re
  let c : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ := HTGeometry.monicMomentAdmissionVector s n
  let dc : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ := xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionVelocity y n
  have hdet : (HTGeometry.momentHankelMatrix s n).det ≠ 0 :=
    ne_of_gt hhead.det_pos
  have hflat' : HTGeometry.momentHankelMatrix s (n + 1) *ᵥ c = 0 := by
    change HTGeometry.momentHankelMatrix
      (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) (n + 1) *ᵥ
        HTGeometry.monicMomentAdmissionVector
          (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) n = 0 at hflat
    simpa only [s, c] using hflat
  have hcurve := hasDerivAt_xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionCurve hy n hdet
  have hmoving := hasDerivAt_xiShiftedMomentInner_movingOddCurrent hy
    (xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionCurve n) dc hcurve
  have hPy : finitePolynomialCurve (xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionCurve n) y =
      HTGeometry.finiteHankelNullPolynomial c := by
    rfl
  have hvelocity :=
    natDegree_finitePolynomialVelocity_xiShiftedCanonicalAdmission_lt hn y
  have hXvelocity :
      (X * finitePolynomialVelocity dc).natDegree < n + 1 := by
    have hsum : 1 + (finitePolynomialVelocity dc).natDegree < 1 + n :=
      Nat.add_lt_add_left hvelocity 1
    calc
      (X * finitePolynomialVelocity dc).natDegree ≤
          X.natDegree + (finitePolynomialVelocity dc).natDegree :=
        Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le
      _ = 1 + (finitePolynomialVelocity dc).natDegree := by
        rw [Polynomial.natDegree_X]
      _ < 1 + n := hsum
      _ = n + 1 := by omega
  have hmovezero : HTGeometry.momentInner s (finitePolynomialVelocity dc)
      (X * HTGeometry.finiteHankelNullPolynomial c) = 0 := by
    have hcomm : HTGeometry.momentInner s (finitePolynomialVelocity dc)
        (X * HTGeometry.finiteHankelNullPolynomial c) =
      HTGeometry.momentInner s (HTGeometry.finiteHankelNullPolynomial c)
        (X * finitePolynomialVelocity dc) := by
      simp only [HTGeometry.momentInner_def]
      congr 1
      ring
    rw [hcomm]
    exact HTGeometry.momentInner_finiteHankelNullPolynomial_eq_zero_of_kernel
      hflat' hXvelocity
  rw [hPy, hmovezero, mul_zero, add_zero] at hmoving
  have hfun :
      (fun v => xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionOddCurrent v n) =
      (fun v => HTGeometry.momentInner
        (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment v k).re)
        (finitePolynomialCurve (xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionCurve n) v)
        (X * finitePolynomialCurve (xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionCurve n) v)) := by
    funext v
    rw [xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionOddCurrent,
      finitePolynomialCurve_xiShiftedCanonicalAdmission]
  rw [hfun]
  have hshear : xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveShear y n =
      HTGeometry.momentInner s (X * HTGeometry.finiteHankelNullPolynomial c)
        (X * xiShiftedBoundaryShiftedEuler 1
          (HTGeometry.finiteHankelNullPolynomial c)) := by
    rfl
  rw [hshear]
  exact hmoving

# Reciprocal-period phase reversal and a flat hypertranscendental boundary

- **ID:** `multiple-elliptic-gamma-reciprocal-rank-flat-phase-reversal`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / RECIPROCAL-PERIOD PHASE CLASSIFICATION / SOURCE-PRODUCED FLAT CLASS
- **Source:** `../3-formalized/all-parameter-multiple-elliptic-gamma-dichotomy.md`;
  `../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/elliptic-gamma-source-face-fracture.md`;
  `../1-in-progress/hypertranscendental-bornological-krull-radical.md`
- **Scientific status:** `[PROVED HERE] [CANDIDATE NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`
  `[EXTERNAL EXACT-MATCH SEARCH NEGATIVE] [NOT AN RH RESULT]`
- **Statement:** Componentwise reciprocalization of a rank-two period family can change its empty
  hypertranscendence graph into a complete graph of arbitrary size.  Along a rational cofinal
  scaling, the resulting hypertranscendental multiple elliptic Gamma functions differ from their
  differentially algebraic zero-nome face by a nonzero all-orders-flat source section.

## Goal

Produce an actual special-function element in the bornological Krull radical, rather than selecting
the ambient witness `exp(-1/|w|)` after the target algebra is known.  The theorem must also detect
genuine differential phase: every finite fibre on one side is differentially algebraic in `z`,
while every reciprocal fibre of order at least one is hypertranscendental in the same variable.

This is a theorem about a reciprocal-period Cremona transform.  It is **not** asserted to be one
global Narukawa modular transformation.  A Jacobi `S`-move on an individual theta face also
rescales `z`, and the different face normalizations do not assemble into one common modular chart.
That non-gluing boundary is part of the result, not silently removed.

## Exact theorem

Fix `N>=2`, distinct integers `n_1,...,n_N`, and a transcendental
`omega` in the complex upper half-plane; one may take `omega=i*pi`.  Put

```text
tau_j=omega+n_j,
alpha_j(m)=tau_j/m,
beta_j(m)=-1/alpha_j(m)=-m/tau_j,              m>=1.       (1)
```

Both period families lie in the upper half-plane.  Let `G_alpha(m)` and `G_beta(m)` be the
`N`-period multiple elliptic Gamma functions in the parity-correct normalization of the
all-parameter dichotomy paper.  Then:

```text
rank_Q span_Q{1,alpha_1(m),...,alpha_N(m)}=2,               (2)
rank_Q span_Q{1,beta_1(m),...,beta_N(m)}=N+1.               (3)
```

Consequently, for every `m`:

```text
G_alpha(m) and its logarithmic derivative are DA over C(z);
G_beta(m) and its logarithmic derivative are HT over C(z). (4)
```

The face law is exact.  Every nonempty face of the `alpha` family is DA.  In the `beta` family,
every singleton face is DA and every face with at least two surviving periods is HT.  Thus
componentwise reciprocalization changes the empty rank-three graph into the complete graph
`K_N`.

For the flat statement, write

```text
q_j(m)=exp(2*pi*i*beta_j(m)),
x(z)=exp(2*pi*i*z),
Q(m)=product_j q_j(m).                                    (5)
```

Let `K` be the closed disk `|z-i|<=1/4`.  Define the DA zero-nome boundary

```text
B_N(z)=1-x(z)          if N is odd,
B_N(z)=1/(1-x(z))     if N is even.                       (6)
```

There are constants `C>0` and `0<r<1`, depending only on the period packet, such that

```text
sup_(z in K) |G_beta(m)(z)-B_N(z)| <= C r^m               (7)
```

for every sufficiently large `m`.  Put `w_m=1/(m+1)` and

```text
A=ell^infinity({m>=1},C(K)),
D_m=G_beta(m)|_K-B_N|_K.                                  (8)
```

After changing finitely many harmless constants in `(7)`, `D` is a bounded sequence and

```text
D != 0,
D belongs to intersection_(k>=1) w^k A.                  (9)
```

In fact every coordinate `D_m` is nonzero.  Hence the actual multiple elliptic Gamma source
supplies a nonzero flat section whose fibres are the difference between an HT function and its
DA boundary.  Every finite inverse-power boundary jet is identical to that of `B_N`, although the
exact fibre remains hypertranscendental.

## Paper proof

### Reciprocal rank

Equation `(2)` is immediate from

```text
alpha_j(m)=omega/m+n_j/m in span_Q{1,omega}.
```

The span has dimension two because `alpha_j(m)` is nonreal.

For `(3)`, suppose

```text
c_0+sum_j c_j/(omega+n_j)=0,                 c_j in Q.    (10)
```

Multiplying by `P(omega)`, where

```text
P(X)=product_j (X+n_j),
```

gives the value at `omega` of a polynomial over `Q`:

```text
c_0 P(X)+sum_j c_j P(X)/(X+n_j).                         (11)
```

Transcendence of `omega` forces this polynomial to vanish identically.  Evaluation at
`X=-n_k` gives

```text
c_k product_(j!=k)(n_j-n_k)=0,
```

so every `c_k` is zero, and then `c_0=0`.  Multiplication by the nonzero rational `-m` does not
change rational rank.  This proves `(3)`, including the same statement for every subpacket.
The exact all-parameter period-rank dichotomy gives `(4)` and the graph classification.

- **ID:** source-event-reciprocal-square-flatness

## Goal

differential required by the reciprocal-square conjecture, rather than merely allowing an

## Setup

Let

\[
A^2=I,\qquad A^\dagger=A,\qquad
U^\dagger U=UU^\dagger=I.
\]

Define source record projection and canonical transmuting map

\[
P=\frac{I-A}{2},\qquad D=UP.                                  \tag{ES1}
\]

Transport the source involution to the target:

\[
A_{\rm out}=UAU^\dagger.                                      \tag{ES2}
\]

Then \(A_{\rm out}\) is again a self-adjoint involution.

## Finite source-event reciprocal-square theorem

`[PROVED HERE]`

The reciprocal squares of the canonical event transfer are

\[
\boxed{
D^\dagger D=P,\qquad
DD^\dagger=\frac{I-A_{\rm out}}2=UPU^\dagger.
}                                                             \tag{ES3}
\]

Consequently, source and target record projections have equal rank.

### Proof

Using unitarity, self-adjointness, and idempotence of \(P\),

/-!
# Noncommutative reciprocal fusion and retained Jordan history

Quadratic congruence gives the exact noncommutative lift of reciprocal direct/reflected formation.
Its flat restriction is the scalar d'Alembert work law.  Away from commuting flats, the missing
coordinate is an explicit commutator history; in a rational algebra it is a sum of double
commutators.  Congruence nonassociativity has an exact ordered associator, while matrix trace
annihilates the Jordan-history sector.

This is the unconditional algebraic core of ULF-RFTM-2.  It contains no RH premise.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

section RingFusion

variable {A : Type*} [Ring A]

/-- Reciprocal work of an invertible formation coordinate. -/
def reciprocalUnitWork (u : Aˣ) : A := (u : A) + (↑u⁻¹ : A) - 2

/-- Quadratic direct formation. -/
def reciprocalDirectFusion (r q : Aˣ) : Aˣ := r * q * r

/-- Quadratic reflected formation. -/
def reciprocalReflectedFusion (r q : Aˣ) : Aˣ := r * q⁻¹ * r

/-- Sum of direct and inverse quadratic congruence actions. -/
def reciprocalCongruenceAction (r : Aˣ) (z : A) : A :=
  (r : A) * z * r + (↑r⁻¹ : A) * z * r⁻¹

/-- One-sided commutator-history correction to radial fusion. -/
def reciprocalCommutatorHistory (r : Aˣ) (z : A) : A :=
  (r : A) * (z * r - r * z) + (↑r⁻¹ : A) * (z * r⁻¹ - r⁻¹ * z)

/-- **Exact noncommutative reciprocal fusion.** -/
theorem reciprocalUnitWork_fusion (r q : Aˣ) :
    reciprocalUnitWork (reciprocalDirectFusion r q) +
      reciprocalUnitWork (reciprocalReflectedFusion r q) =
        reciprocalCongruenceAction r (reciprocalUnitWork q) +
          2 * reciprocalUnitWork (r * r) := by
  simp [reciprocalUnitWork, reciprocalDirectFusion, reciprocalReflectedFusion,
    reciprocalCongruenceAction]
  noncomm_ring

/-- Congruence splits into a radial term and a one-sided commutator history. -/
theorem reciprocalCongruenceAction_commutator_decomposition (r : Aˣ) (z : A) :
    reciprocalCongruenceAction r z =
      (((r * r : Aˣ) : A) + (↑(r * r)⁻¹ : A)) * z +
        reciprocalCommutatorHistory r z := by
  simp [reciprocalCongruenceAction, reciprocalCommutatorHistory]
  noncomm_ring

/-- The history correction vanishes on every commuting flat. -/
theorem reciprocalCommutatorHistory_eq_zero_of_commute (r : Aˣ) (z : A)
    (h : (r : A) * z = z * r) :
    reciprocalCommutatorHistory r z = 0 := by
  have hinv : (↑r⁻¹ : A) * z = z * r⁻¹ := by
    calc
      (↑r⁻¹ : A) * z = (↑r⁻¹ : A) * z * 1 := by simp
      _ = (↑r⁻¹ : A) * z * ((r : A) * r⁻¹) := by simp
      _ = (↑r⁻¹ : A) * (z * r) * r⁻¹ := by noncomm_ring
      _ = (↑r⁻¹ : A) * ((r : A) * z) * r⁻¹ := by rw [h]
      _ = ((↑r⁻¹ : A) * r) * z * r⁻¹ := by noncomm_ring
      _ = z * r⁻¹ := by simp
  simp [reciprocalCommutatorHistory, h, hinv]

/-- On a commuting flat, noncommutative fusion collapses to the scalar reciprocal fusion law. -/
theorem reciprocalUnitWork_radial_fusion (r q : Aˣ)
    (h : (r : A) * reciprocalUnitWork q = reciprocalUnitWork q * r) :
    reciprocalUnitWork (reciprocalDirectFusion r q) +
      reciprocalUnitWork (reciprocalReflectedFusion r q) =
        reciprocalUnitWork (r * r) * reciprocalUnitWork q +
          2 * reciprocalUnitWork (r * r) + 2 * reciprocalUnitWork q := by
  rw [reciprocalUnitWork_fusion, reciprocalCongruenceAction_commutator_decomposition,
    reciprocalCommutatorHistory_eq_zero_of_commute r (reciprocalUnitWork q) h]
  simp [reciprocalUnitWork]
  noncomm_ring

/-- Quadratic congruence as the ordered formation operation. -/
def reciprocalCongruenceFusion (r q : Aˣ) : Aˣ := r * q * r

/-- **Exact associator.**  Ordered history is the commutator of successive half-formations. -/
theorem reciprocalCongruenceFusion_associator (s r q : Aˣ) :
    (reciprocalCongruenceFusion s (reciprocalCongruenceFusion r q) : A) -
        reciprocalCongruenceFusion (s * r) q =
      (s : A) * r * q * ((r : A) * s - s * r) := by
  simp [reciprocalCongruenceFusion]
  noncomm_ring

end RingFusion
