/-- Canonical reader of the new top coordinate born at one Tate stage. -/
def tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient
    (m : ℕ) (v : Fin (m + 2) → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  v (Fin.last (m + 1))

/-- Reciprocal flat-minus-scaled Tate anomalies, assembled as one rank-two odd matrix. -/
def tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix
    (a : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ :=
  !![0,
      -tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient m
        (tateClockFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect (Real.exp a : ℂ) m
          (tateClockFinIntervalBasis ℂ (Fin.last m)));
    -tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient m
        (tateClockFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect (Real.exp (-a) : ℂ) m
          (tateClockFinIntervalBasis ℂ (Fin.last m))),
      0]

/-- The forward Tate top anomaly recovers the forward Gamma suspension leg without loss. -/
theorem tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient_flatMinusRaw_exp
    (a : ℝ) (m : ℕ) :
    -tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient m
        (tateClockFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect (Real.exp a : ℂ) m
          (tateClockFinIntervalBasis ℂ (Fin.last m))) =
      (sourceHorizontalGammaSixUnitForwardBoundaryDefect a : ℂ) := by
  rw [tateClockFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect_eq_topBoundary,
    tateClockFinIntervalTopBoundary_basis_last]
  simp [tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient,
    tateClockFinIntervalBasis,
    sourceHorizontalGammaSixUnitForwardBoundaryDefect_eq]

/-- The reflected Tate top anomaly recovers the reciprocal Gamma suspension leg without loss. -/
theorem tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient_flatMinusRaw_exp_neg
    (a : ℝ) (m : ℕ) :
    -tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient m
        (tateClockFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect (Real.exp (-a) : ℂ) m
          (tateClockFinIntervalBasis ℂ (Fin.last m))) =
      (sourceHorizontalGammaSixUnitReflectedBoundaryDefect a : ℂ) := by
  rw [tateClockFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect_eq_topBoundary,
    tateClockFinIntervalTopBoundary_basis_last]
  simp [tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient,
    tateClockFinIntervalBasis,
    sourceHorizontalGammaSixUnitReflectedBoundaryDefect_eq]

/-- Completion reconstruction: reciprocal Tate naturality defects recover exactly the Gamma
curved suspension, hence transported reflection minus bare reflection. -/
theorem tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix_eq_curvedSuspension
    (a : ℝ) (m : ℕ) :
    tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix a m =
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixCurvedSuspension a := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  · simp [tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixCurvedSuspension,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixForwardSuspensionLeg,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixReflectedSuspensionLeg]
  · simpa [tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixCurvedSuspension,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixForwardSuspensionLeg,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixReflectedSuspensionLeg] using
        (tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient_flatMinusRaw_exp a m)
  · simpa [tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixCurvedSuspension,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixForwardSuspensionLeg,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixReflectedSuspensionLeg] using
        (tateClockCofinalTopCoefficient_flatMinusRaw_exp_neg a m)
  · simp [tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixCurvedSuspension,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixForwardSuspensionLeg,
      sourceHorizontalGammaSixReflectedSuspensionLeg]

/-- Completion Clifford law: the paired naturality anomaly squares to scalar curvature. -/
theorem tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix_sq
    (a : ℝ) (m : ℕ) :
    tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix a m *
        tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix a m =
      -(sourceHorizontalGammaSixUnitOppositeBoundaryCurvature a : ℂ) •
        (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) := by
  rw [tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix_eq_curvedSuspension,
    sourceHorizontalGammaSixCurvedSuspension_sq]

/-- Determinant of the paired completion anomaly is the positive Gamma curvature. -/
theorem det_tateClockRelativeReflectionCofinalCoefficientMatrix
    (a : ℝ) (m : ℕ) :

congr 1

/-- Naturality defect of an integral finite Tate arrow scaled by a Laurent clock gain. -/
def deningerIntegralTateScaledForwardNaturalityDefect
    (gain : DeningerIntegralTateRing) (m : ℕ)
    (f : Fin (m + 1) → DeningerIntegralTateRing) :
    Fin (m + 2) → DeningerIntegralTateRing :=
  (gain • deningerIntegralTateIntervalForward (m + 1))
      (deningerIntegralTateIntervalInclusion (m + 1) f) -
    deningerIntegralTateIntervalInclusion (m + 1)
      ((gain • deningerIntegralTateIntervalForward m) f)

theorem deningerIntegralTateScaledForwardNaturalityDefect_eq_topBoundary
    (gain : DeningerIntegralTateRing) (m : ℕ)
    (f : Fin (m + 1) → DeningerIntegralTateRing) :
    deningerIntegralTateScaledForwardNaturalityDefect gain m f =
      gain • deningerIntegralTateIntervalTopBoundary m f := by
  simp only [deningerIntegralTateScaledForwardNaturalityDefect,
    LinearMap.smul_apply, map_smul]
  rw [deningerIntegralTateIntervalForward_inclusion_defect]
  module

/-- Flat-minus-scaled integral cofinal defect. -/
def deningerIntegralTateFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect
    (gain : DeningerIntegralTateRing) (m : ℕ)
    (f : Fin (m + 1) → DeningerIntegralTateRing) :
    Fin (m + 2) → DeningerIntegralTateRing :=
  deningerIntegralTateScaledForwardNaturalityDefect 1 m f -
    deningerIntegralTateScaledForwardNaturalityDefect gain m f

theorem deningerIntegralTateFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect_eq_topBoundary
    (gain : DeningerIntegralTateRing) (m : ℕ)
    (f : Fin (m + 1) → DeningerIntegralTateRing) :
    deningerIntegralTateFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect gain m f =
      (1 - gain) • deningerIntegralTateIntervalTopBoundary m f := by
  rw [deningerIntegralTateFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect,
    deningerIntegralTateScaledForwardNaturalityDefect_eq_topBoundary,
    deningerIntegralTateScaledForwardNaturalityDefect_eq_topBoundary]
  module

/-- Canonical integral reader of the newly born top coordinate. -/
def deningerIntegralTateTopCoefficient
    (m : ℕ) (v : Fin (m + 2) → DeningerIntegralTateRing) :
    DeningerIntegralTateRing := v (Fin.last (m + 1))

/-- Paired flat-versus-`T` and flat-versus-`T⁻¹` Tate anomalies. -/
def deningerIntegralTateRelativeReflectionCoefficientMatrix
    (m : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) DeningerIntegralTateRing :=
  !![0,
      -deningerIntegralTateTopCoefficient m
        (deningerIntegralTateFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect
          (1 + deningerIntegralCartierSourceGenerator) m
          (deningerIntegralTateIntervalBasis (Fin.last m)));
    -deningerIntegralTateTopCoefficient m
        (deningerIntegralTateFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect
          (1 + inversion ℤ deningerIntegralCartierSourceGenerator) m
          (deningerIntegralTateIntervalBasis (Fin.last m))),
      0]

theorem deningerIntegralTateTopCoefficient_flatMinusRaw
    (gain : DeningerIntegralTateRing) (m : ℕ) :
    -deningerIntegralTateTopCoefficient m
        (deningerIntegralTateFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect gain m
          (deningerIntegralTateIntervalBasis (Fin.last m))) = gain - 1 := by
  rw [deningerIntegralTateFlatMinusRawCofinalDefect_eq_topBoundary,
    deningerIntegralTateIntervalTopBoundary_basis_last]
  simp [deningerIntegralTateTopCoefficient,
    deningerIntegralTateIntervalBasis]

/-- Source-level completion reconstruction: canonical top readout of reciprocal integral clock
defects is exactly the universal integral relative-reflection matrix. -/
theorem deningerIntegralTateRelativeReflectionCoefficientMatrix_eq
    (m : ℕ) :
    deningerIntegralTateRelativeReflectionCoefficientMatrix m =
      deningerIntegralRelativeReflectionDifferential := by
  apply Matrix.ext
  intro i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  · simp [deningerIntegralTateRelativeReflectionCoefficientMatrix,
      deningerIntegralRelativeReflectionDifferential]
  · simpa [deningerIntegralTateRelativeReflectionCoefficientMatrix,
      deningerIntegralRelativeReflectionDifferential,
      deningerIntegralCartierSourceGenerator] using
        (deningerIntegralTateTopCoefficient_flatMinusRaw
          (1 + deningerIntegralCartierSourceGenerator) m)
  · simpa [deningerIntegralTateRelativeReflectionCoefficientMatrix,
      deningerIntegralRelativeReflectionDifferential] using
        (deningerIntegralTateTopCoefficient_flatMinusRaw
          (1 + inversion ℤ deningerIntegralCartierSourceGenerator) m)
  · simp [deningerIntegralTateRelativeReflectionCoefficientMatrix,
      deningerIntegralRelativeReflectionDifferential]

/-- Algebraic direct sum of reciprocal orientation packets over all Tate stages. -/
abbrev DeningerIntegralCofinalTateOrientationPacket :=
  ℕ →₀ (Fin 2 → DeningerIntegralTateRing)

/-- Global integral relative-reflection operator, acting stagewise on the cofinal direct sum. -/
def deningerIntegralCofinalRelativeReflectionOperator :
    DeningerIntegralCofinalTateOrientationPacket →ₗ[DeningerIntegralTateRing]
      DeningerIntegralCofinalTateOrientationPacket :=
  Finsupp.mapRange.linearMap

(x : H) :
    ((vG.quotientZeroSubgroupEquivValueSubgroup
        (QuotientGroup.mk' vG.zeroSubgroup (N.toHom x)) : vG.valueSubgroup) :
      Multiplicative ℤ) ∈
      integerMultipleSubgroup (N.residueDegree : ℤ) :=
  N.quotientZeroSubgroup_value_mem_integerMultipleSubgroup_of_mem_normSubgroup
    ((MonoidHom.mem_range (f := N.toHom)).2 ⟨x, rfl⟩)

/--
Establishes the membership statement `((vG.quotientZeroSubgroupEquivValueSubgroup
(QuotientGroup.mk' vG.zeroSubgroup (x / y)) : vG.valueSubgroup) : Multiplicative ℤ) ∈
integerMultipleSubgroup (N.residueDegree : ℤ)`.
-/
theorem quotientZeroSubgroup_value_div_mem_integerMultipleSubgroup_of_div_mem_normSubgroup
    {x y : G} (hxy : x / y ∈ N.normSubgroup) :
    ((vG.quotientZeroSubgroupEquivValueSubgroup
        (QuotientGroup.mk' vG.zeroSubgroup (x / y)) : vG.valueSubgroup) :
      Multiplicative ℤ) ∈
      integerMultipleSubgroup (N.residueDegree : ℤ) :=
  N.quotientZeroSubgroup_value_mem_integerMultipleSubgroup_of_mem_normSubgroup
    hxy

/-- If a quotient is a norm, then the valuation difference is divisible by the
residue degree. -/
theorem residueDegree_dvd_valuation_difference_of_div_mem_normSubgroup
    {x y : G} (hxy : x / y ∈ N.normSubgroup) :
    (N.residueDegree : ℤ) ∣ vG.val x - vG.val y := by
  have h := N.residueDegree_dvd_valuation_of_mem_normSubgroup hxy
  simpa [vG.val_div] using h

/-- Explicit multiple form of
`residueDegree_dvd_valuation_difference_of_div_mem_normSubgroup`. -/
theorem exists_valuation_difference_eq_residueDegree_mul_of_div_mem_normSubgroup
    {x y : G} (hxy : x / y ∈ N.normSubgroup) :
    ∃ n : ℤ, vG.val x - vG.val y = (N.residueDegree : ℤ) * n :=
  N.residueDegree_dvd_valuation_difference_of_div_mem_normSubgroup hxy

/-- Right-multiple form of the valuation difference forced by norm-subgroup
membership of a quotient. -/
theorem exists_valuation_difference_eq_mul_residueDegree_of_div_mem_normSubgroup
    {x y : G} (hxy : x / y ∈ N.normSubgroup) :
    ∃ n : ℤ, vG.val x - vG.val y = n * (N.residueDegree : ℤ) := by
  rcases
    N.exists_valuation_difference_eq_residueDegree_mul_of_div_mem_normSubgroup
      hxy with ⟨n, hn⟩
  exact ⟨n, by rw [hn, mul_comm]⟩

/-- If a quotient is represented by the norm of a specific element, its
valuation difference is computed by that element's valuation. -/
theorem valuation_difference_eq_residueDegree_mul_of_norm_eq_div
    {x y : G} {z : H} (hz : N.toHom z = x / y) :
    vG.val x - vG.val y = (N.residueDegree : ℤ) * vH.val z := by
  calc
    vG.val x - vG.val y = vG.val (x / y) := (vG.val_div x y).symm
    _ = vG.val (N.toHom z) := by rw [← hz]
    _ = (N.residueDegree : ℤ) * vH.val z := N.valuation_apply z

/-- Right-multiple form of
`valuation_difference_eq_residueDegree_mul_of_norm_eq_div`. -/
theorem valuation_difference_eq_mul_residueDegree_of_norm_eq_div
    {x y : G} {z : H} (hz : N.toHom z = x / y) :
    vG.val x - vG.val y = vH.val z * (N.residueDegree : ℤ) := by
  rw [N.valuation_difference_eq_residueDegree_mul_of_norm_eq_div hz,
    mul_comm]

/-- A norm-subgroup element is a valuation-zero factor times the norm of a
source-uniformizer power.  This is the abstract normal form behind local CFT
norm quotient calculations; no surjectivity on units is assumed. -/
theorem exists_zeroSubgroup_mul_norm_uniformizer_zpow_eq_of_mem_normSubgroup
    {ϖH : H} (hϖH : vH.IsUniformizer ϖH)
    {x : G} (hx : x ∈ N.normSubgroup) :
    ∃ u : G, u ∈ vG.zeroSubgroup ∧
      ∃ n : ℤ, x = u * N.toHom (ϖH ^ n) := by
  rcases N.residueDegree_dvd_valuation_of_mem_normSubgroup hx with ⟨n, hn⟩
  have hval :
      vG.val x = vG.val (N.toHom (ϖH ^ n)) := by
    rw [N.valuation_apply_uniformizer_zpow hϖH n, hn]
  rcases vG.exists_zeroSubgroup_mul_eq_of_val_eq hval with ⟨u, hu, hux⟩
  exact ⟨u, hu, n, hux.symm⟩

/-- If all valuation-zero target elements are norms and the source valuation
has a uniformizer, valuation divisibility by the residue degree is sufficient
for norm-subgroup membership. -/
theorem mem_normSubgroup_of_residueDegree_dvd_val_of_zeroSubgroup_le
    {ϖH : H} (hϖH : vH.IsUniformizer ϖH)
    (hzero : vG.zeroSubgroup ≤ N.normSubgroup)
    {x : G} (hx : (N.residueDegree : ℤ) ∣ vG.val x) :
    x ∈ N.normSubgroup := by
  rcases hx with ⟨n, hn⟩
  have hval :
      vG.val x = vG.val (N.toHom (ϖH ^ n)) := by
    rw [N.valuation_apply_uniformizer_zpow hϖH n, hn]
  rcases vG.exists_zeroSubgroup_mul_eq_of_val_eq hval with ⟨u, hu, hux⟩
  have hu_norm : u ∈ N.normSubgroup := hzero hu
  have hnorm : u * N.toHom (ϖH ^ n) ∈ N.normSubgroup :=
    N.normSubgroup.mul_mem hu_norm
      ((MonoidHom.mem_range (f := N.toHom)).2 ⟨ϖH ^ n, rfl⟩)
  simpa [← hux] using hnorm

/-- With source uniformizer and norm-surjectivity on valuation-zero target
elements, the norm subgroup is exactly the elements whose valuation is
divisible by the residue degree. -/
theorem mem_normSubgroup_iff_residueDegree_dvd_val_of_zeroSubgroup_le
    {ϖH : H} (hϖH : vH.IsUniformizer ϖH)

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.DifferenceAwayLocalization

/-!
# Existence of a Picard--Vessiot ring for a linear difference system

Putting the previous layers together: the coordinate ring of a fundamental matrix, localized at its
determinant, is a difference ring carrying an invertible formal fundamental solution of the system
`σ Y = A Y`; quotienting by a maximal `σ`-ideal makes it `σ`-simple without destroying the
fundamental matrix.  The result is a Picard--Vessiot ring: a `σ`-simple difference ring, generated
over the base by the entries of an invertible fundamental matrix and the inverse of its
determinant, whose constants form a field.

This is the foundation on which a difference Galois group can be defined, and it exists in neither
mathlib nor the rest of this repository.
-/

open MvPolynomial

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-! ### The abstract existence statement -/

/-- **Existence of a Picard--Vessiot quotient of a difference ring with a fundamental matrix.**
A nontrivial difference ring carrying an invertible fundamental solution matrix of a linear system
has a `σ`-simple quotient in which the matrix is still an invertible fundamental solution, and the
constants of that quotient form a field. -/
theorem exists_picardVessiot_of_fundamentalMatrix
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Nontrivial S] (τ : S ≃+* S)
    {n : ℕ} (B Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) S)
    (hY : ∀ i j, τ (Y i j) = (B * Y) i j) (hdet : IsUnit Y.det) :
    ∃ (M : Ideal S) (hM : IsSigmaIdeal τ M) (_ : M ≠ ⊤) (hM' : IsSigmaIdeal τ.symm M),
      IsSigmaSimple (sigmaQuotientEquiv τ M hM hM') ∧
      IsField (sigmaConstantsSubring (sigmaQuotientEquiv τ M hM hM')) ∧
      (∀ i j, sigmaQuotientEquiv τ M hM hM' (Ideal.Quotient.mk M (Y i j))
        = ((B.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk M)) * (Y.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk M))) i j) ∧
      IsUnit (Y.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk M)).det := by
  classical
  have hbot : IsSigmaIdeal τ (⊥ : Ideal S) := isSigmaIdeal_bot τ
  have hbotne : (⊥ : Ideal S) ≠ ⊤ := bot_ne_top
  obtain ⟨M, hIM, hM, hMne, hmax⟩ := exists_maximal_isSigmaIdeal τ (⊥ : Ideal S) hbot hbotne
  have hM' : IsSigmaIdeal τ.symm M := isSigmaIdeal_symm_of_maximal hM hMne hmax
  have hsimple : IsSigmaSimple (sigmaQuotientEquiv τ M hM hM') :=
    isSigmaSimple_quotient_of_maximal hM hMne hmax
  haveI : Nontrivial (S ⧸ M) := by
    rw [← not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial, Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff]
    exact hMne
  refine ⟨M, hM, hMne, hM', hsimple,
    isField_sigmaConstantsSubring_of_isSigmaSimple hsimple, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i j
    have hmk : sigmaQuotientEquiv τ M hM hM' (Ideal.Quotient.mk M (Y i j))
        = Ideal.Quotient.mk M (τ (Y i j)) := rfl
    rw [hmk, hY i j]
    simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.map_apply, map_sum]
  · have hmap : (Y.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk M)).det = Ideal.Quotient.mk M Y.det := by
      rw [RingHom.map_det (Ideal.Quotient.mk M) Y, RingHom.mapMatrix_apply]
    rw [hmap]
    exact hdet.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk M)

/-! ### The concrete Picard--Vessiot ring of an invertible system -/

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}

/-- The determinant of the generic matrix is a nonzero polynomial: it takes the value one at the
identity matrix. -/
theorem fundamentalMatrix_det_ne_zero :
    (fundamentalMatrix K n).det ≠ 0 := by
  classical
  set e : Fin n × Fin n → K := fun p => if p.1 = p.2 then 1 else 0 with he
  have hmap : (fundamentalMatrix K n).map (MvPolynomial.eval e)
      = (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) := by
    refine Matrix.ext fun i j => ?_
    simp [fundamentalMatrix, Matrix.map_apply, Matrix.one_apply, he]
  have heval : MvPolynomial.eval e ((fundamentalMatrix K n).det) = 1 := by
    rw [RingHom.map_det (MvPolynomial.eval e) (fundamentalMatrix K n),
      RingHom.mapMatrix_apply, hmap, Matrix.det_one]
  intro hzero
  rw [hzero, map_zero] at heval
  exact zero_ne_one heval

/-- The `σ`-action on the coordinate ring, as an explicit ring homomorphism on the inverse side. -/
theorem sigmaCoordEquiv_symm_apply (σ : K ≃+* K) (A A' : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)
    (hAA' : A * A' = 1) (hA'A : A' * A = 1) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) K) :
    (sigmaCoordEquiv σ A A' hAA' hA'A).symm p =
      sigmaCoordHom σ.symm (A'.map (σ.symm : K →+* K)) p := rfl

variable (σ : K ≃+* K) (A A' : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)

/-- The coordinate ring of a fundamental matrix, localized at its determinant. -/
abbrev pvLocalization (K : Type*) [Field K] (n : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  Localization.Away ((fundamentalMatrix K n).det)

theorem powers_fundamentalDet_le_nonZeroDivisors :
    Submonoid.powers ((fundamentalMatrix K n).det) ≤
      nonZeroDivisors (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) K) := by
  rintro x ⟨k, rfl⟩
  refine mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero ?_
  exact pow_ne_zero k fundamentalMatrix_det_ne_zero

instance : Nontrivial (pvLocalization K n) := by
  have hinj : Function.Injective
      (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) K) (pvLocalization K n)) :=

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ObserverRecurrenceDistributionLaw

/-!
# The stationary recurrence quotient law

Every survival-return experiment on a stationary quantum spectrum factors
through two canonical information quotients:

* the system spectrum is replaced by its energy-difference law;
* the clock law is replaced by its reflection-even orientation quotient.

The theorem below identifies the complete sampled return probability law
with the pushforward pairing of exactly these two quotients.  It applies to
arbitrary real probability spectra and arbitrary probability clocks.
-/

open MeasureTheory

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The survival fidelity carried by the system's energy-difference law. -/
def recurrenceQuotientFidelity
    (mu : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu] (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (charFun (spectralDifferenceMeasure mu) t).re

/-- Probability-law pairing of the maximal system and clock recurrence
quotients. -/
def recurrenceQuotientProbabilityMeasure
    (clockLaw : ProbabilityMeasure ℝ)
    (mu : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu] :
    ProbabilityMeasure ℝ :=
  ProbabilityMeasure.map
    (clockOrientationQuotientLaw clockLaw)
    (f := recurrenceQuotientFidelity mu)
    (by
      exact
        (Complex.continuous_re.comp
          continuous_charFun).aemeasurable)

/-- The quotient fidelity is exactly the original survival fidelity. -/
theorem recurrenceQuotientFidelity_eq_normSq_charFun
    (mu : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu] (t : ℝ) :
    recurrenceQuotientFidelity mu t =
      Complex.normSq (charFun mu t) := by
  rw [recurrenceQuotientFidelity,
    charFun_spectralDifferenceMeasure]
  simp

/-- **Universal stationary recurrence quotient law.**  For every
probability energy spectrum and every probability clock, the complete
sampled survival-return distribution is the pushforward of the clock's
orientation quotient by the characteristic function of the system's
energy-difference law. -/
theorem clockSampledSpectralReturnProbabilityMeasure_eq_recurrenceQuotient
    (clockLaw : ProbabilityMeasure ℝ)
    (mu : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu] :
    (clockSampledSpectralReturnProbabilityMeasure
        clockLaw mu : Measure ℝ) =
      (recurrenceQuotientProbabilityMeasure
        clockLaw mu : Measure ℝ) := by
  have horientation :
      (clockSampledSpectralReturnProbabilityMeasure
          clockLaw mu : Measure ℝ) =
        (clockSampledSpectralReturnProbabilityMeasure
          (clockOrientationQuotientLaw clockLaw) mu :
            Measure ℝ) := by
    apply
      (clockSampledSpectralReturnProbabilityMeasure_eq_iff_moments
        clockLaw (clockOrientationQuotientLaw clockLaw)
        mu mu).2
    intro n
    rw [clockSampledSpectralReturnMoment_orientationQuotient]
  rw [horientation]
  rw [clockSampledSpectralReturnProbabilityMeasure,
    recurrenceQuotientProbabilityMeasure,
    ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure_map,
    ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure_map]
  apply Measure.map_congr
  filter_upwards with t
  exact (recurrenceQuotientFidelity_eq_normSq_charFun
    mu t).symm

end

end RHTower

/-!
# The Picard--Vessiot ring of a difference system has no new constants

Assembling the two halves: the localized coordinate ring of a fundamental matrix is a finite-type
algebra over the base, its quotient by a maximal `σ`-ideal is `σ`-simple, and a `σ`-simple
finite-type extension of a difference field with algebraically closed constants has exactly the
constants of the base.

So the Picard--Vessiot ring of any invertible linear difference system is a `σ`-simple difference
ring, containing an invertible fundamental solution matrix, whose constants are exactly those of
the base field.  That is the full defining property of a Picard--Vessiot ring.
-/

open Polynomial

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}

theorem algebraMap_pvLocalization (x : K) :
    algebraMap K (pvLocalization K n) x =
      algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) K) (pvLocalization K n) (MvPolynomial.C x) := by
  rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) K) (pvLocalization K n)]
  rfl

theorem pvSigma_algebraMap (σ : K ≃+* K) (A A' : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)
    (hAA' : A * A' = 1) (hA'A : A' * A = 1) (x : K) :
    pvSigma σ A A' hAA' hA'A (algebraMap K (pvLocalization K n) x)
      = algebraMap K (pvLocalization K n) (σ x) := by
  rw [algebraMap_pvLocalization, algebraMap_pvLocalization]
  rw [pvSigma]
  rw [sigmaAwayEquiv_algebraMap]
  congr 1
  exact sigmaCoordHom_C σ A x

/-- **The Picard--Vessiot ring of an invertible linear difference system has no new constants.**
Its constants are exactly the constants of the base field, provided those are infinite and
algebraically closed. -/
theorem exists_picardVessiot_no_new_constants (σ : K ≃+* K) (A A' : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)
    (hAA' : A * A' = 1) (hA'A : A' * A = 1)
    (hinf : ((differenceConstants σ : Subfield K) : Set K).Infinite)
    (hclosed : ∀ g : K[X], g.Monic → 0 < g.natDegree → g.map (σ : K →+* K) = g →
      ∃ a : K, σ a = a ∧ g.IsRoot a) :
    ∃ (M : Ideal (pvLocalization K n))
      (hM : IsSigmaIdeal (pvSigma σ A A' hAA' hA'A) M) (_ : M ≠ ⊤)
      (hM' : IsSigmaIdeal (pvSigma σ A A' hAA' hA'A).symm M),
      IsSigmaSimple (sigmaQuotientEquiv (pvSigma σ A A' hAA' hA'A) M hM hM') ∧
      (∀ i j, sigmaQuotientEquiv (pvSigma σ A A' hAA' hA'A) M hM hM'
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk M (pvFundamental K n i j))
        = (((A.map (pvBaseMap K n)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk M)) *
            ((pvFundamental K n).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk M))) i j) ∧
      IsUnit ((pvFundamental K n).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk M)).det ∧
      (∀ x : (pvLocalization K n) ⧸ M,
        sigmaQuotientEquiv (pvSigma σ A A' hAA' hA'A) M hM hM' x = x →
          ∃ a : K, σ a = a ∧ x = algebraMap K ((pvLocalization K n) ⧸ M) a) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hMne, hM', hsimple, hfield, hfund, hdet⟩ :=
    exists_picardVessiot_system σ A A' hAA' hA'A
  refine ⟨M, hM, hMne, hM', hsimple, hfund, hdet, ?_⟩
  haveI : Nontrivial ((pvLocalization K n) ⧸ M) := by
    rw [← not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial, Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff]
    exact hMne
  haveI : Algebra.FiniteType K ((pvLocalization K n) ⧸ M) :=
    Algebra.FiniteType.of_surjective (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K M) Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective
  have hcompat : ∀ x : K,
      sigmaQuotientEquiv (pvSigma σ A A' hAA' hA'A) M hM hM'
          (algebraMap K ((pvLocalization K n) ⧸ M) x)
        = algebraMap K ((pvLocalization K n) ⧸ M) (σ x) := by
    intro x
    have hmk : ∀ y : K, algebraMap K ((pvLocalization K n) ⧸ M) y
        = Ideal.Quotient.mk M (algebraMap K (pvLocalization K n) y) := fun _ => rfl
    rw [hmk, hmk, sigmaQuotientEquiv_mk, pvSigma_algebraMap]
  intro x hx
  exact exists_eq_algebraMap_of_isSigmaSimple σ
    (sigmaQuotientEquiv (pvSigma σ A A' hAA' hA'A) M hM hM') hcompat hsimple hinf hclosed hx

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ParameterizedDifferenceGalois

/-!
# A derivation descends to the quotient by a differential ideal

The parameterized theory needs the quotient of a `σ`-`δ` ring by an ideal stable under both
operators to be a `σ`-`δ` ring again.  The difference operator descends because the ideal is a
`σ`-ideal; this file supplies the other half, which mathlib does not have: a derivation of a
commutative ring descends to the quotient by any ideal it preserves.

The construction is the universal property of the quotient applied to `x ↦ [δ x]`, which kills the
ideal exactly because the ideal is `δ`-stable; the Leibniz rule then transfers on representatives.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Differential R]

/-- The descended derivation, as a function on the quotient. -/
def quotDerivFun (I : Ideal R) (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, Differential.deriv x ∈ I) (z : R ⧸ I) : R ⧸ I :=
  Quotient.liftOn' z (fun x : R => (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (Differential.deriv x))
    (by
      intro a b hab
      have hmem : a - b ∈ I := by
        rwa [Submodule.quotientRel_def] at hab
      have hderiv : Differential.deriv a - Differential.deriv b ∈ I := by
        have := hI _ hmem
        rwa [map_sub] at this
      exact (Ideal.Quotient.eq).mpr hderiv)

@[simp] theorem quotDerivFun_mk (I : Ideal R) (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, Differential.deriv x ∈ I) (x : R) :
    quotDerivFun I hI (Ideal.Quotient.mk I x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk I (Differential.deriv x) := rfl

/-- The descended derivation, as an additive homomorphism. -/
def quotDerivAddHom (I : Ideal R) (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, Differential.deriv x ∈ I) :
    (R ⧸ I) →+ (R ⧸ I) :=
  AddMonoidHom.mk' (quotDerivFun I hI)
    (by
      intro z w
      induction z using Quotient.inductionOn' with
      | h a =>
        induction w using Quotient.inductionOn' with
        | h b =>
          show quotDerivFun I hI (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (a + b))
            = quotDerivFun I hI (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a)
              + quotDerivFun I hI (Ideal.Quotient.mk I b)
          rw [quotDerivFun_mk, quotDerivFun_mk, quotDerivFun_mk, map_add, map_add])

/-- **A derivation descends to the quotient by a differential ideal.** -/
def quotDeriv (I : Ideal R) (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, Differential.deriv x ∈ I) :
    Derivation ℤ (R ⧸ I) (R ⧸ I) where
  toLinearMap := (quotDerivAddHom I hI).toIntLinearMap
  map_one_eq_zero' := by
    show quotDerivFun I hI (Ideal.Quotient.mk I 1) = 0
    rw [quotDerivFun_mk, Derivation.map_one_eq_zero, map_zero]
  leibniz' := by
    intro z w
    induction z using Quotient.inductionOn' with
    | h a =>
      induction w using Quotient.inductionOn' with
      | h b =>
        show quotDerivFun I hI (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (a * b))
          = Ideal.Quotient.mk I a • quotDerivFun I hI (Ideal.Quotient.mk I b)
            + Ideal.Quotient.mk I b • quotDerivFun I hI (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a)
        rw [quotDerivFun_mk, quotDerivFun_mk, quotDerivFun_mk, Derivation.leibniz, map_add]
        simp only [smul_eq_mul, map_mul]

/-- The quotient of a differential ring by a differential ideal is a differential ring. -/
@[reducible] def quotientDifferential (I : Ideal R) (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, Differential.deriv x ∈ I) :
    Differential (R ⧸ I) := ⟨quotDeriv I hI⟩

theorem quotientDifferential_deriv_mk (I : Ideal R) (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, Differential.deriv x ∈ I)
    (x : R) :
    @Differential.deriv _ _ (quotientDifferential I hI) (Ideal.Quotient.mk I x)
      = Ideal.Quotient.mk I (Differential.deriv x) := rfl

/-- **The quotient by a maximal doubly stable ideal is a difference-differential ring.**  The
difference operator descends because the ideal is a `σ`-ideal in both directions, and the derivation
descends because the ideal is a `δ`-ideal; the two descended operators still commute. -/
theorem quotientDifferential_commutesDeriv {σ : R ≃+* R} (hσ : CommutesDeriv σ)
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsSigmaDeltaIdeal σ I) (hI' : IsSigmaIdeal σ.symm I) :
    @CommutesDeriv (R ⧸ I) _ (quotientDifferential I hI.2)
      (sigmaQuotientEquiv σ I hI.1 hI') := by
  intro z
  induction z using Quotient.inductionOn' with
  | h a =>
    show sigmaQuotientEquiv σ I hI.1 hI'
        (@Differential.deriv _ _ (quotientDifferential I hI.2) (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a))
      = @Differential.deriv _ _ (quotientDifferential I hI.2)
        (sigmaQuotientEquiv σ I hI.1 hI' (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a))
    rw [quotientDifferential_deriv_mk, sigmaQuotientEquiv_mk, sigmaQuotientEquiv_mk,
      quotientDifferential_deriv_mk, hσ a]

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
